`71fcc965504a51e68508a1bf947f172b43a24b1a3df67194f62ad0ee130f22a2`

## 2026-08-24 — Join public CloudFormation trust to administrator authority

**Coverage gap and primary semantics.** The scanner's native infrastructure
models covered Kubernetes host and cluster authority, but not AWS identity
configuration. CloudFormation represents role trust in
[`AWS::IAM::Role.AssumeRolePolicyDocument`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-iam-role.html).
AWS documents that a wildcard principal permits every principal of the stated
type, that role trust and caller identity policies interact differently for
same- and cross-account callers, and that the managed
[`AdministratorAccess`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/AdministratorAccess.html)
policy allows every action on every resource. Permissions boundaries cap the
maximum identity-policy permission rather than granting permission themselves;
the same unrestricted AdministratorAccess policy used as a boundary therefore
does not reduce this role. See AWS's [`Principal` element](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_elements_principal.html),
[permissions-boundary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_boundaries.html),
and [policy-evaluation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic.html)
documentation.

**Comparative lesson.** Trivy deliberately normalizes multiple infrastructure
formats into one representation, a useful direction for later cross-format
coverage. For this increment, retain native CloudFormation syntax so exact
lines and fail-closed intrinsic values remain auditable. A public Checkov issue
records a concrete false positive where a wildcard principal was constrained
by a trust condition. That failure mode is more important than broad keyword
coverage: a wildcard principal, administrator policy, or wildcard action alone
must never become the complete finding. See [Trivy misconfiguration
scanning](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy/blob/main/docs/guide/scanner/misconfiguration/index.md),
[Trivy checks contribution model](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy-checks/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md),
and [Checkov issue 7304](https://github.com/bridgecrewio/checkov/issues/7304).

**Chosen precision boundary.** Emit `cloudformation-public-admin-role` only
when one exact `AWS::IAM::Role` joins both halves. Its trust must contain an
unrestricted `Allow`, `Principal: "*"` or AWS-principal `"*"`, and
case-insensitive `sts:AssumeRole`, `sts:*`, or `*`. Its permission side must
contain the exact AdministratorAccess ARN for the commercial, China, or GovCloud
partition, or an inline unrestricted `Allow` whose action and resource each
contain `"*"`. Preserve logical ID, optional literal RoleName, role type,
principal, action, condition state, permission form, boundary state,
CWE-269/CWE-284, and exact source/sink lines. An absent boundary and the exact
AdministratorAccess boundary are both explicitly recorded as unbounded.

**Parser and false-positive boundary.** Parse only `.yaml`, `.yml`, `.json`,
and `.template` source as strict YAML 1.2 with unique mapping keys; JSON is a
strict subset. Recognize CloudFormation shorthand intrinsic tags so unrelated
outputs or metadata do not invalidate an otherwise static role, while an
intrinsic or other dynamic value at a modeled principal, action, permission, or
boundary fails closed. Reject aliases anywhere, malformed documents, invalid
policy versions, non-template shapes, ambiguous statement and policy shapes,
duplicate inline-policy identities, nonempty or dynamic trust or inline-policy
conditions, `NotAction`/`NotPrincipal`/`NotResource`, specific principals,
narrower actions or resources, and every other static or dynamic permissions
boundary. This deliberately misses parameter-resolved public roles and
semantically permissive custom managed policies until exact resolution can be
added without guessing. Empty condition maps remain unrestricted rather than
being credited as a control. When no immutable model inventory is available,
fallback traversal admits `.json` and `.template` files only after a bounded
content prefilter observes both a Resources mapping and `AWS::IAM::Role`.
Adding every JSON file to the shared source set displaced existing framework
rows under the 8 MiB/2,000-file budgets and bypassed an oversized npm-boundary
control in the first full regression run; the format-specific prefilter retains
arbitrarily named CloudFormation JSON without spending the application and
package-analysis budget on unrelated metadata.

**Deployment and attack-path discipline.** Static template evidence proves a
declared source-level authority defect, not an active role or successful
session. The exact joined chain is nevertheless reportable with unchanged
deployment and caller permission stated as conditional preconditions. An
attacker who controls an external AWS account can create or control an AWS
principal and grant its caller-side `sts:AssumeRole` permission; the target
repository need not contain that attacker's credential. Correction must reopen
the role and inspect repository-visible template selection, transforms, macros,
nested stacks, StackSets, CDK/SAM synthesis, overlays, and effective controls.
Missing deployment telemetry, current role state, target account identity, or a
named caller is remaining uncertainty, not suppression evidence. Only positive
repository or runtime evidence that the stack is excluded or rejected, the role
does not exist, rendering replaces the policy, or an effective control closes
the chain is deployment counterevidence. The different same- and cross-account
trust rules, applicable SCPs, session policies, permissions boundaries,
explicit denies, MFA/external-ID conditions, drift, and current role state
calibrate confidence and realized impact. Report the least concrete conditional
secret, IAM, data, workload, persistence, billing, or destructive capability;
do not infer anonymous internet access, active deployment, valid credentials, a
successful session, or organization-wide compromise from a template alone.

**Effectiveness gate.** The positive fixture attaches AdministratorAccess to a
role with a wildcard AWS principal and no trust condition. Its source-identical
control changes only the principal to one account root. The dedicated manifest
holds completion, precision, recall, F1, stable detection, validation,
attack-path, code-evidence, severity, and negative-control gates at perfection
with zero false positives. Eight focused groups cover exact row identity,
YAML/JSON/template parsing, CloudFormation tags, all AWS partitions, managed and
inline permission forms, empty versus effective conditions, unbounded versus
restrictive boundaries, narrower authority, malformed and ambiguous input, and
reviewer guidance. The focused and canonical lanes pass 26 tests and 1,748
assertions on native Windows and Ubuntu/WSL. The canonical benchmark advances
to 103 exploit/control pairs, 206 cases, and 618 repeated scans.

**Final acceptance.** At exact implementation checkpoint
`77546af1ad18746790e4fb3c5d3f90c2f1f285fb`, the authoritative Windows Bun
1.3.14 suite passes 1,516 tests and 11,252 assertions across 168 files in 581.48
seconds, with 20 intentional environment/platform skips and no failures. The
first full run's two failures were valuable acceptance evidence: general JSON
ingestion reduced the decompression model's retained repository rows from the
required 169 to 166 and let a child source cross an oversized npm package
boundary. After the format-specific prefilter, both exact suites pass on
Windows and Ubuntu/WSL while an arbitrarily named nested CloudFormation JSON
template remains detected. Generated-model drift, formatting, TypeScript, a
clean production build, and the high-severity production audit are green.

## 2026-08-24 — Preserve broad-principal Kubernetes cluster-admin grants

**Coverage gap and primary semantics.** The first native Kubernetes model joins
container and host filesystem authority, but does not cover control-plane
authorization. Kubernetes defines a ClusterRoleBinding as a cluster-wide grant,
documents that the built-in `cluster-admin` role provides full control over
every cluster resource, and specifically warns that binding it to
`system:serviceaccounts` lets any application act as a cluster administrator.
Its authentication documentation assigns every successful identity to
`system:authenticated` and unauthenticated requests to `system:anonymous` plus
`system:unauthenticated`; RBAC good practices recommend removing unauthenticated
bindings where possible. See [Kubernetes RBAC
authorization](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/rbac/),
[Kubernetes authentication](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/),
and [Kubernetes RBAC good
practices](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/rbac-good-practices/).

**Chosen precision boundary.** Emit
`kubernetes-cluster-admin-broad-subject` only for an exact strict-YAML
`rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1` ClusterRoleBinding whose immutable `roleRef`
names the built-in ClusterRole `cluster-admin` and whose exact User or Group is
one of `system:anonymous`, `system:unauthenticated`,
`system:authenticated`, or `system:serviceaccounts`. Preserve the binding name,
API, cluster scope, principal kind/name, role reference, CWE-269/CWE-284, and
exact lines. Support multi-document YAML and v1 List objects through the same
parser as the hostPath model.

**Fail-closed and false-positive boundary.** Named administrator groups,
individual or default ServiceAccounts, namespace-scoped
`system:serviceaccounts:<namespace>` groups, RoleBindings, custom or similarly
named roles, beta/wrong APIs, metadata namespaces, namespaces on User or Group
subjects, duplicate subject identities, aliases, duplicate YAML keys, malformed
documents, and non-YAML files do not emit. This deliberately misses equivalent
custom wildcard ClusterRoles until a later model can resolve exact rules and
aggregation without turning syntax breadth into an impact claim. It also does
not label every intentional cluster administrator as vulnerable.

**Deployment and attack-path discipline.** A static binding proves declared
authority, not that an API server admits it or that an attacker possesses the
principal. Correction must verify rendered selection, deployed object, exact
roleRef and subject, RBAC in the effective authorizer chain, then the relevant
reachability boundary: anonymous-auth configuration and API network access,
valid authenticated credentials, or a realistically obtainable service-account
token. RBAC grants are additive, so a separate narrow binding does not subtract
the dangerous grant. If deployed, identify the least concrete secret read,
workload creation, RBAC change, namespace action, or node-related effect instead
of inventing public exposure or token theft.

**Effectiveness gate.** The positive fixture uses the exact Kubernetes warning
shape: built-in cluster-admin bound to `system:serviceaccounts`. Its source-
identical control changes only the binding identity and subject to one named
platform-administrator group. The dedicated manifest holds completion,
precision, recall, F1, stable detection, validation, attack-path, code-evidence,
severity, and negative-control gates at perfection with zero false positives.
Seven focused groups pass 36 assertions. The combined Kubernetes and canonical
lane passes 31 tests and 1,768 assertions on native Windows and Ubuntu/WSL. The
canonical benchmark advances to 102 exploit/control pairs, 204 cases, and 612
repeated scans.

seconds, with 20 intentional platform/environment skips and no failures.

build, and the production dependency audit are green. Two compiled inventories

581,530 bytes with SHA-256
`ac1d024e3486aa3f80fa49c066b12acae2690c5ed831f36bb69d7d7aa8ae6281`.
Exactly one RBAC row preserves `Group:system:serviceaccounts`, the built-in
cluster-admin role reference, binding identity, cluster scope, and exact lines;

its matched control is absent, showing that both Kubernetes models survive the

Windows and Ubuntu/WSL strictly inspect the same POSIX-built 255-entry,

`51ef028caad7dca0b75315a0ca15d694fabd45af6aa34bf3ce2e52fc6e4e4caa`.

## 2026-08-24 — Join Kubernetes privilege and host filesystem authority

**Coverage gap and comparative evidence.** Application dataflow, package
advisories, GitHub Actions, secrets, and imported SARIF already had deterministic
host assistance, but Terraform, Kubernetes, CloudFormation, and Helm had no
native semantic model. Trivy treats those formats as first-class
misconfiguration inputs and ships separate Kubernetes checks for privileged
containers and mounted host paths. Kubernetes itself says privileged containers
receive all Linux capabilities and override seccomp, AppArmor, and SELinux
constraints; its volume guidance warns that a read-write hostPath can subvert
the host mount; and its Baseline Pod Security Standard forbids privileged
containers and hostPath volumes. See [Trivy misconfiguration
scanning](https://trivy.dev/docs/dev/scanner/misconfiguration/), [Kubernetes
privileged-container semantics](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/linux-kernel-security-constraints/#privileged-containers),
[Kubernetes hostPath guidance](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/volumes/#hostpath),
and the [Pod Security Standards](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/).

**Chosen precision boundary.** Do not reproduce two independent presence
warnings. Emit `kubernetes-privileged-sensitive-hostpath` only after joining an
exact supported workload API/kind, its PodSpec, one exact Linux container in
`containers`, `initContainers`, or `ephemeralContainers`, boolean
`securityContext.privileged: true`, one uniquely named sensitive absolute
hostPath volume, and a matching absolute read-write volumeMount on that same
container. Preserve exact workload/name/namespace, container section/name,
volume identity, normalized effective host path after a literal safe subPath,
mount path, and source/sink lines. The model covers Pod,
ReplicationController, apps/v1 Deployment/DaemonSet/ReplicaSet/StatefulSet,
batch/v1 Job/CronJob, multi-document YAML, and v1 List objects.

**Fail-closed and control boundary.** YAML 1.2 parsing is strict and rejects
aliases, duplicate mapping keys, malformed documents, unsupported or mismatched
API/kind pairs, missing workload identity, duplicate volume/container names,
nonboolean security values, unresolved or duplicate volume references,
nonabsolute mounts, dynamic subPath expressions, parent-escaping subpaths, and
non-YAML lookalikes. Read-only mounts and nonsensitive effective subpaths close
the modeled write chain. Explicit `hostUsers: false` closes this host-namespace
authority model because Kubernetes maps container root and capabilities away
from the host namespace; Windows PodSpecs and Windows node selectors are outside
the Linux privileged field's schema. See [Kubernetes user
namespaces](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/pods/user-namespaces/).
Do not credit `readOnlyRootFilesystem`, `runAsNonRoot`,
`allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, AppArmor, SELinux, or seccomp as silently
repairing a privileged container or a separate writable host mount.

**Model review and impact discipline.** The structured row is a high-priority
host-authority hypothesis, not proof of a remote attacker. The correction turn
must establish that rendered configuration retains the row, the workload is
actually admitted and deployed, no non-exempt Baseline/Restricted policy rejects
it, and a concrete principal, remotely exploitable process, untrusted image or
plugin, compromised dependency, or exec permission reaches the container. It
must then identify the exact host file, socket, runtime, credential, persistence,
or privilege effect. Without that evidence, node takeover and cluster/control-
plane compromise are not reportable conclusions.

**Effectiveness gate.** The positive fixture is an apps/v1 Deployment with one
pinned image, boolean privileged mode, a unique host-root volume, and a
read-write `/host` mount. The matched control preserves workload purpose and
image but uses `hostUsers: false`, boolean nonprivileged mode, and an isolated
emptyDir. The dedicated manifest requires perfect completion, precision,
recall, F1, case and negative-control behavior, stable detection, validation,
attack-path, code-evidence and severity coverage, with zero false positives.
Seven focused groups pass 42 assertions. The combined focused and canonical
lane passes 24 tests and 1,721 assertions on native Windows and Ubuntu/WSL.
Two native whole-repository inventories are byte-identical at the 256-row cap
with SHA-256
`51c2c9907f8e8a5bc2e0c1c355616a2cea830afbfe0754d456529048062c6844`;
exactly one Kubernetes row survives for the vulnerable fixture and none for the
control. The canonical benchmark now contains 101 exploit/control pairs, 202
cases, and 606 repeated scans.

**Final local acceptance and portable packaging.** The authoritative Windows
Bun 1.3.14 suite passes 1,501 tests and 11,163 assertions across 166 files in
705.07 seconds, with 20 intentional platform/environment skips and no failures.
Generated-model drift, formatting, TypeScript checking, and the clean
production build pass; `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` reports no known
vulnerabilities. Windows and Ubuntu/WSL strictly inspect the same 255-entry,
1,800,859-byte npm archive with SHA-256
`63f03c3a436d5fbf1baf752af50ab670e219fff1a8b2c9f18cb1b68cd75798b5`.

## 2026-08-24 — Resume host-audited correction after complete-draft transport loss

**Measured gap.** The immutable self-scan established that a late Copilot
transport loss can leave all three draft artifacts present but 415 of 417
inventory paths without exact direct-file closure. The client converted that
state into `CompleteDraftArtifactsError`, deliberately excluded the error from
ordinary fresh-session retry, and let the API invoke deterministic
finalization. A correction-turn transport break was weaker still: the client
emitted `quality_gate_incomplete` and reported `turn.completed` whenever the
draft files still existed. The finalizer correctly refused to invent coverage,
but the orchestrator had abandoned useful bounded correction capacity.

**Dedicated recovery phase.** Inspect only the cause of a complete-draft
signal. When it is the scanner-owned model deadline or a sanitized transport
interruption, schedule the next isolated session as
`draft_quality_correction` inside the existing configured fresh-session
budget. That session skips the full initial scan prompt and starts with the
mandatory quality gate, freshly rebuilding residual-risk, secret-candidate,
coverage-gap, and finding-quality inventories from the current drafts and
immutable repository inputs. A repeated retryable transport loss remains in
the correction phase until the shared one-to-five-session budget is exhausted.
The final failure then retains the complete-draft signal for deterministic
host handling. Never extend this classification to authentication,
authorization, safety, sandbox, contract, cancellation, or arbitrary model
errors.

**Cross-session evidence invariant.** Successful built-in `view` completions
are host telemetry about the same staged, repository-read-only snapshot, so
preserve their exact normalized inventory paths across session replacement.
Pending tool calls are not evidence and are scoped to one session. Clear them
before each replacement session; otherwise a colliding tool-call ID could turn
an old interrupted view into a false success. Shell reads, model coverage
labels, receipts, and summaries still cannot populate the host evidence set.
Final inventory-digest verification continues to bind the staged snapshot
before sealing.

**Observability and regression evidence.** Fresh-session events carry only the
bounded retry reason plus `scan` or `draft_quality_correction`; API observers
validate that phase and the CLI explains it without provider text. Unit tests
cover timeout-to-correction transition, repeated timeout/transport correction,
shared-budget exhaustion behavior, non-retryable causes, stale tool-call-ID
reuse, and phase rendering. The deterministic recovery benchmark starts with
three apparently closed coverage rows: one successful first-session view
leaves two gaps, a stale completion after replacement leaves both gaps, and two
exact replacement-session views reduce the host gap count to zero. Focused
Windows acceptance passes 142 tests and 1,378 assertions with one intentional
skip; the corresponding WSL/Linux lane passes with only its intentional
Windows-launcher skip.

**Final acceptance.** The authoritative Windows Bun 1.3.14 suite passes 1,494
tests and 11,110 assertions across 165 files in 647.36 seconds, with 20
intentional platform/environment skips and no failures. Generated-model drift,
repository formatting, TypeScript checking, and a clean production build are
green; the production audit reports no known vulnerabilities. Windows and
Linux strictly inspect the same 251-entry, 1,810,430-byte npm archive with
SHA-256
`e994930f48909f8153e5cdc4e4a63fada70deaab425c2376c0dfa39d98ab39e9`.
Their isolated consumers install 67 and 75 packages respectively and validate
the public import, CLI, and all 79 bundled plugin files. The archive and
isolated installation directories are removed after acceptance.

**Hosted acceptance.** All exact-source workflow families pass on checkpoint
`bc97e5e4bde3f9d8c6637113d38f6b63ef8c2b55`: Node `32796785950`, container
`32796785902`, Windows GUI `32796785918`, Linux GUI `32796785931`, Java

Windows Node 22, macOS Node 22, and Linux Node 22, 24, 24.0.0, 26, and 26.0.0.

**Hosted deadlock guards are not scanner deadlines.** A subsequent
documentation-head Windows run completed 1,492 tests without an assertion
failure but the hosted Python interpreter exceeded the test's 30-second
subprocess guard and private credential-home setup exceeded its 60-second outer
guard. Preserve the distinction between a scanner model-turn deadline and a
test-process deadlock bound. The two slow environment integrations now allow

credential-home preparation. No production timeout, retry budget, assertion,

The corresponding WSL audit exposed an independent mounted-filesystem timing
assumption in the split TypeScript npm-bin integration: a clean build plus two

## 2026-08-24 — Make imported-analyzer closure a sealed host fact

**Gap and external semantics.** SARIF interchange increases recall only if the
scanner can prove what happened to every imported result. The SARIF 2.1.0
standard distinguishes a result that is absent from the current run and gives
suppressions explicit status semantics; GitHub uses partial fingerprints for
result identity and supports a bounded SARIF subset; Sonar imports external
issues while keeping the external producer's conclusion distinct from its own
analysis. These sources support treating SARIF as candidate evidence, but none
lets this scanner inherit a producer's finding or claim imported coverage from
prose alone. See the [OASIS SARIF 2.1.0
specification](https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/os/sarif-v2.1.0-os.html),
[GitHub CodeQL SARIF output
guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/codeql/codeql-cli/sarif-output),
[GitHub's supported SARIF
subset](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/code-security/reference/code-scanning/sarif-files/sarif-support),
and [Sonar external-issue
imports](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-server/analyzing-source-code/importing-external-issues).

**Trusted binding and reconciliation.** Bind all four launch-recipe fields as
one atomic contract: source paths, normalized candidate count, the SHA-256 of
the exact candidate JSONL bytes, and ordered source IDs/digests. Registration
rejects partial bindings, zero or excessive candidates, excessive sources,
non-lowercase hashes, and nonsequential source IDs. Completion rereads bounded,
no-follow scan-local files, verifies the source metadata and candidate bytes
against that immutable binding, derives scope from the host inventory, and
matches the reserved instance plus exact CWE/location identity against the
enriched ledger. Missing, duplicate, invented, out-of-scope, or identity-
mutated rows fail closed. Each in-scope row must have terminal validation;
reportable or deferred validation also needs a consistent attack-path decision.

**Receipt, completeness, and tamper evidence.** The host—not the model—writes
`artifacts/03_coverage/external_sarif_seed_coverage.json`. It records input,
source-metadata, and enriched-ledger digests; one input-ordered terminal
`reportable`, `rejected`, `deferred`, or `out_of_scope` row per normalized
seed; and exact totals. Canonical coverage references the source metadata,
candidate JSONL, ledger, and receipt, causing all four to enter the manifest
seal. Deferred seeds add deterministic deferred work and force partial
coverage. Re-finalization recomputes the receipt and coverage records and
byte-compares them with the sealed state, so post-prepare mutation fails. The
SDK exposes the receipt path, while CLI and desktop completion warnings expose
the counts without trusting model prose.

**Effectiveness gate.** `expectedSeedCoverage` upgrades the dedicated seeded
command-injection/safe-command pair from a findings-only check to a closure
contract. The evaluator requires consistent totals, unique reserved instances,
the canonical coverage reference, and the exact receipt digest in the scan
manifest. The positive must be reportable and the noisy negative rejected;
either deferred work, a missing seed, or an unsealed receipt makes the run
incomplete. Adversarial regressions cover partial and malformed recipe
bindings, missing/duplicate/invented/out-of-scope/mutated rows, inconsistent
validation and attack-path states, candidate/source tampering, and sealed
ledger mutation. This establishes a reusable receipt contract for future
opt-in analyzer adapters without coupling the core scanner to their execution.

**Cross-mode closure compatibility.** The first live deep runs correctly found
the vulnerable seed and rejected the safe seed, but exposed a host/model
contract mismatch: deep scans keep validation and attack-path rows in separate
ledgers and may preserve imported identities in bounded merged forms rather
than the compact standard row. The host now recognizes exact top-level and
single-level imported-seed records, canonical snake/camel location fields, and
the observed reserved-instance aliases. It never searches arbitrary recursive
text or accepts a same-family neighbor. Exactly one representation must match
the immutable instance, CWE list, and normalized locations; duplicate,
conflicting, incomplete, or identity-mutated aliases fail closed. Separate
validation and attack-path ledgers are read only when needed, bound by
candidate identity, included in the closure receipt, referenced by canonical
coverage, and sealed in the manifest. A reportable or deferred row needs both
terminal agreement and substantive attack-path evidence; a rejected row needs
independent validation but no invented attack path. Deep and diff prompts now
prefer one canonical imported-seed row, keeping compatibility in the host as a
recovery boundary rather than an output-format target.

**Live positive and negative evidence.** A fresh Copilot deep scan of the
vulnerable seeded command fixture sealed one reportable seed, emitted the one
expected high finding, and passed completion, precision, recall, F1, stable
detection, validation, attack-path, code-evidence, severity, and case gates

The safe run completed on its first attempt after compatibility hardening. This
pair demonstrates that the receipt measures both recovered recall and explicit
false-positive rejection rather than merely accepting a model-authored finding.

**Compatibility hardening acceptance.** Final review also rejects mixed valid

## 2026-08-24 — Bind shell-quote object-token escaping to real POSIX dispatch

**Selection and comparative gap.** [GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p / CVE-2026-9277](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w7jw-789q-3m8p) affects `shell-quote` 1.1.0 through 1.8.3. Its object-token serializer escaped `op` with a dot-based replacement that does not match LF, CR, U+2028, or U+2029; a line terminator can therefore survive serialization and become a command separator in a POSIX shell. Release 1.8.4 instead accepts only the operator values the parser itself emits. Authenticated public-source search found no advisory or CVE reference in CodeQL and nine `shell-quote` references; the inspected examples parse a command and feed a shell-free `execFileSync` argv boundary rather than modeling attacker-shaped object-token serialization. Public Semgrep rules contain no advisory, CVE, or package reference. The initial current-reference search returned no advisory or CVE and one package reference before GitHub throttled subsequent queries; locally available comparison snapshots contain only unrelated prose and predate the advisory. Among reviewed candidates, this advisory offered the strongest new precision boundary: dependency version, unusual object-token shape, exact serializer identity, and a real shell dispatch must all coincide.

**Executable boundary before implementation.** Install official 1.8.3 and 1.8.4 in isolated roots. Direct `{ op: externalValue }` construction and a `parse(command, envFn)` callback returning the same object both retain the line terminator on 1.8.3; 1.8.4 rejects each with `invalid \`op\` value`. Ordinary remote string tokens remain single-quoted in both versions. ## 2026-08-24 — Bind node-tar decompression amplification to reachable compressed input

**Coverage gap and upstream boundary.** [GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw / CVE-2026-59873](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-23hp-3jrh-7fpw) describes critical resource exhaustion when node-tar processes compressed input without a cumulative output bound. `maxReadSize` limits an individual read, not total decompressed bytes. The official [7.5.19 repair](https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar/commit/2812e9338665659b183aa7226518c307044957d3) counts compressed and decompressed bytes in the parser and defaults `maxDecompressionRatio` to 1000 for gzip, brotli, and zstd. Authenticated searches found neither the advisory identifier nor `maxDecompressionRatio` in the official CodeQL repository, public Semgrep rules, or the reference scanner. Dependency scanners can identify `tar <=7.5.18`, but not whether remote compressed bytes reach a consuming parser or whether the application lists, parses, or extracts them.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add `node-http-tar-decompression-dos` only for an official namespace/default or TypeScript receiver, named or aliased `t`/`list`/`x`/`extract`/`Parse`/`Unpack`, CommonJS receiver/destructure, or direct require member. Require a remote request/upload value in the options `file`, a dynamic options object, or a request stream piped directly into the operation, plus nearest exact production or fresh root-declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 proof through 7.5.18. Record list, parse, and extraction operations separately because parser throughput/event-loop effects do not prove disk consumption. Reject fixed archives, create APIs, patched or prerelease versions, wrong and development-only packages, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent or v1 locks, reassigned bindings, replaced members, wrapper shadows, and local lookalikes. Keep ratio/output/entry/time/quota/concurrency markers as reviewer-visible control leads; do not credit `maxReadSize`, `maxDepth`, or a small compressed upload limit as a cumulative expansion bound.

**Shared dependency-proof correction.** The focused negative matrix exposed that npm v2/v3 evidence checked exact root declaration equality between `package.json` and the lock, but accepted a hand-crafted resolved version below a simple caret or tilde minimum. The shared resolver now applies the existing semantic inclusion check to exact/caret/tilde declarations before accepting the installed version. This removes stale-lock false positives for the common declaration forms across all package-aware models without pretending the lightweight parser understands every complex registry range; unsupported complex syntax retains the prior behavior pending a complete bounded range evaluator.

**Benchmark and executable evidence.** Add source-identical four-file fixtures with three relative-import wrapper boundaries. The positive pins tar 7.5.18 and the control changes only the dependency to 7.5.19; both include complete npm v3 locks and the same self-checking witness. The witness constructs an 8,390,144-byte tar containing zeros and compresses it to 8,242 bytes without extracting it. The affected parser completes the 1017.97:1 expansion. The repaired parser aborts at an observed ratio of 1001.88 against its default 1000 limit. An exact-commit inventory then exposed legitimate cross-advisory contamination in the older linkpath negative control: tar 7.5.11 fixes that control's link primitive but remains affected by decompression. Upgrade only that control's package evidence to 7.5.21, preserving application source and the original link repair while also closing decompression and member-filter recursion; a regression requires it to remain absent from the new model. The perfect-gate pair advances the canonical corpus to 92 exploit/control pairs, 184 cases, and 552 repeated scans. Focused regressions prove official binding shapes, file and stream sources, operation-specific provenance, version and lock boundaries, binding integrity, paired source identity, reviewer guidance, retained control evidence, and cross-family negative isolation. **Consequence.** The scanner now distinguishes dependency presence from a reachable compressed-input parser and distinguishes parser/listing availability pressure from extraction effects. ## 2026-08-24 — Require remote JSONata expressions to reach evaluation before claiming RCE

**Coverage gap and version contract.** Three newly reviewed critical advisories describe distinct but overlapping ways for JSONata expressions to escape intended lookup boundaries: `$clone` overwrite and procedure application in [GHSA-66mm-25pp-rfff](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-66mm-25pp-rfff), a bypassable `hasOwnProperty` check in [GHSA-2943-5xfg-gq5f](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2943-5xfg-gq5f), and a missing own-property check in [GHSA-8gq3-vp5j-2grp](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8gq3-vp5j-2grp). Their complete union is below 1.8.8 plus 2.0.0 through 2.2.0; 1.8.8 and 2.2.1 are the first releases on their respective lines that close all three chains. Current authenticated source searches of the official CodeQL repository, Semgrep rules, and the reference scanner find no JSONata application model. Package alerts can identify an affected version, but cannot prove that an attacker controls the expression rather than only the data being queried, or that a compiled expression is ever evaluated.

**Executable behavior before pattern matching.** Isolated official packages establish a bounded, non-shell sentinel: `( $hasOwnProperty := $spread($string); $__proto__ := $constructor; $constructor("return process.version")() )`. JSONata 1.8.7 and 2.2.0 recover the host `Function` constructor and return the running Node version. Source-identical 1.8.8 and 2.2.1 stop at `T1006`, “Attempted to invoke a non-function.” This proves a host-capability boundary without spawning a command, touching the filesystem, opening a listener, or making a network request. An initial managed install attempt was deliberately abandoned when package installation was not explicitly rooted in its isolated temporary directory; the accepted harness verifies and enters the exact temporary path before installation and removes that path afterward.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add `node-http-jsonata-expression-rce` only when remote request data reaches argument zero of an official JSONata compiler and the compiler's exact result reaches `.evaluate()`. Resolve stable default aliases, namespace `.default`, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS callables, an inline `require("jsonata")` callable, and a stable one-hop compiler alias. Accept an immediate evaluation chain or a retained compiled expression, including multiline compiler and member calls, and record the evaluation line rather than the earlier compilation line. Require nearest exact production metadata or a fresh root-declaration-consistent npm lock/shrinkwrap v2/v3 resolution. Carry that proof through same-file and cross-file summaries as a `jsonata-runtime-dependency` propagator. Fail closed on patched or non-stable versions, wrong or development-only packages, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent or v1 locks, package presence alone, compile-only use, a fixed expression with request data supplied only to `evaluate`, named-import or CommonJS-default guesses, local lookalikes, parameter shadowing, binding or compiled-object reassignment, namespace-default or `evaluate` replacement, and test/example paths. The quality gate must reproduce an expression against the installed build, establish actual `process`, `global`, `Function`, or equivalent host access, and connect that capability to a specific command, filesystem, network, secret, or availability effect. Advisory membership alone is never an RCE finding.

**Benchmark and initial evidence.** Add source-identical Express fixtures with three relative-import wrapper boundaries. The positive pins JSONata 2.2.0 and the control changes only that dependency to 2.2.1. Both include complete npm locks and the same self-checking witness. The scanner preserves request source `src/server.js:8`, wrapper topology, actual evaluation sink `src/storage.js:6`, CWE-94, and `jsonata@2.2.0:manifest-exact:expression-sandbox-escape`; the repaired twin emits no model row. The strict diagnostic and canonical manifests retain perfect precision, recall, validation, attack-path, code-evidence, severity, and stability gates. Focused regressions cover supported factory shapes, immediate and retained evaluation, multiline syntax, both release-line boundaries, exact and locked provenance, capability mutation, source-position confusion, path exclusions, repository candidate pressure, fixture topology, and reviewer guidance. The new pair advances the canonical corpus to 91 exploit/control pairs, 182 cases, and 546 three-run scans. ## 2026-08-24 — Fail closed when Auth.js configuration fails

**Selection and scanner comparison.** [GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3 / CVE-2026-73421](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8fpg-xm3f-6cx3) is a high-value application-aware target: affected Auth.js v5 applications can silently treat every unauthenticated visitor as authenticated when a deployment error occurs, but only if application code also relies on the bare auth object's existence. This lets the scanner improve on package-presence alerts by proving both vulnerable runtime provenance and the application decision. Authenticated repository-scoped source searches found no advisory identifier in the official CodeQL or public Semgrep rules repositories. CodeQL has two `next-auth` references: a hard-coded-credential test and a Next.js framework model whose only Auth.js-specific behavior is the factory's `secret` member as a secret sink. The public Semgrep rules repository has no `next-auth` reference. This establishes a current application-model gap, not a claim that dependency scanners miss the affected package.

**Repair semantics and prerelease provenance.** In 5.0.0-beta.31, each `auth()` entry point obtains a session `Response` from Auth.js core and calls `.json()` without checking its status. A provider missing both `issuer` and `authorization`, an absent required secret, or another server configuration failure produces status 500 with a JSON `{message}` body. The wrapper assigns that truthy object to `req.auth` or returns it as the session. The official repair commit introduces one `parseSessionResponse` helper, returns `null` whenever `response.ok` is false, and routes RSC, middleware, API-route, and wrapper paths through it; the published repair is 5.0.0-beta.32. The general Node dependency prover previously accepted only stable `major.minor.patch` exact pins and stable-character ranges. Extend it to canonical SemVer prereleases/build metadata and to prerelease-bearing registry-range syntax only when a declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock supplies the exact installed version. Git, URL, npm-alias, workspace, tag-only, unlocked, inconsistent, and v1-lock declarations remain outside the trust boundary.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add `node-authjs-configuration-error-fail-open` with source `unauthenticated-authjs-request-during-configuration-error`, sink `vulnerable-next-auth-truthy-error-object-authorization-decision`, and CWE-636/CWE-285. Require a stable official default, namespace-default, TypeScript import-equals, or CommonJS `next-auth` factory; its generated stable `auth` wrapper; and a concrete access-control consequence using the bare object directly, through destructuring, through a derived boolean, or through a no-argument `auth()` result. Also preserve the official Next.js 16 form where `callbacks.authorized` returns a bare auth boolean and a proxy, middleware, or default export actually deploys that generated wrapper; declaring an unused callback is not reachability. Preserve same-file and relative-import paths plus a unique same-manifest `@/` or `~/` root-alias target; ambiguity fails closed. Exact affected production pins and fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 resolutions are accepted. Repaired/v4/wrong/development-only packages, unresolved ranges, reassignment, ambiguous aliases, undeployed callbacks, local lookalikes, tests/examples, log-only truthiness, and wrapper enrichment without a decision stay negative. `auth.user`, a stable user identifier, role, or permission is strong counterevidence for this specific error-object condition, while its correctness for broader authorization remains a separate review question.

**Published-package oracle and benchmark.** Source-identical fixtures contain the same provider configuration, generated wrapper, middleware, and witness; only exact `next-auth` 5.0.0-beta.31 versus 5.0.0-beta.32 locks differ. The witness constructs a synthetic request and incomplete OIDC provider without opening a listener or issuing an outbound request. Bun executes the packages' real wrapper and core code. Beta.31 logs `InvalidEndpoints`, supplies a truthy error object, and returns 204; beta.32 logs the same configuration error, supplies `null`, and returns 401. Nine focused groups pass 36 assertions across official bindings, the full published beta boundary, exact and lock-resolved prerelease proof, direct/destructured/aliased/no-argument decisions, official authorized-callback proxy exports, unique and ambiguous root aliases, hard negatives, source identity, strict manifest gates, and reviewer guidance. The new perfect-gate pair advances the corpus to 90 exploit/control pairs, 180 cases, and 540 three-run scans. Full cross-platform, scanner, package, GUI, self-review, and hosted acceptance follow the implementation checkpoint.

**Final scanner and package acceptance.** Exact implementation checkpoint `cd70d9fdf3593aee6e2bbafb62f03a5185597a0f` passes the authoritative Bun 1.3.14 suite with 1,390 tests, 10,595 assertions, 20 intentional environment/platform skips, zero failures, and a 360.39-second runtime across 155 files. Generated-model drift, repository-wide formatting, TypeScript compilation, a separate clean production build, the production-only high-severity audit, and both Windows and Ubuntu/WSL real-package witnesses are green. The witness instructions now name Bun explicitly: direct Node ESM currently rejects the package's extensionless `next/server` import, while Bun executes the published wrapper and core code on both hosts. Beta.31 consistently reports `allowed:true`, status 204, a non-null truthy error body, and no listener; beta.32 reports `allowed:false`, status 401, null auth, and no listener.

Two compiled inventories of a clean exact-HEAD archive take 31,748.603 and 11,600.654 ms and produce 96 byte-identical rows, 241,719 bytes, and SHA-256 `ded03793bc5be9cb870749038650cabc440a6ceadd1029a2597aee90e99ffa7d`; 92 rows are rooted in benchmark fixtures. The only `node-authjs-configuration-error-fail-open` row retains the exact source at `benchmarks/fixtures/node-authjs-configuration-error-fail-open/src/middleware.ts:4`, authorization-decision sink at line 5, CWE-636/CWE-285, and `next-auth@5.0.0-beta.31:manifest-exact:truthy-configuration-error-auth-object` provenance. Managed-sandbox full-suite attempts were discarded when Bun could not read pnpm content-store hardlinks and native ACL/Git operations were denied; the affected generated `yauzl` hardlinks were replaced with byte-identical ordinary files, and the authoritative native run passed. **Consequence.** Future authentication models should retain this two-sided proof: establish the framework's actual failure value and the application's exact authorization interpretation. A vulnerable dependency is not enough, and a bare auth-object check is not enough without affected runtime provenance. Conversely, deployment misconfiguration is an explicit attack requirement rather than a reason to suppress a demonstrated fail-open path. Findings must describe the concrete unauthenticated route or operation and must not infer execution, disclosure, or privilege beyond that evidence.

## 2026-08-24 — Bind node-opcua username tokens to the active session nonce

**Selection and independently verified repair boundary.** [GHSA-mq36-523m-x7vv / CVE-2026-54155](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mq36-523m-x7vv) identifies missing cryptographic verification in `node-opcua` username authentication. This is a better application-aware increment than a dependency-only product advisory because the scanner can prove a narrow sequence: application code imports the official aggregate, constructs a server with a real user manager, exposes an encrypted username-token policy, and starts that exact instance. Public official CodeQL and Semgrep rule-source searches did not identify a node-opcua username-token model; that is evidence of an application-model gap, not a claim that dependency scanners miss the package. The advisory's reviewed range ends at 2.165.0, so release chronology alone was not used to broaden it. Exact published `node-opcua-server` archives for 2.165.0, 2.165.1, and 2.165.2 were inspected and all contain the same vulnerable extraction: decrypt the blob, subtract `session.nonce.length` from its declared length, and pass the resulting password to `isValidUser` without checking trailing bytes. Exact 2.166.0 introduces `extractPasswordFromDecryptedBlob`, rejects negative or truncated lengths, and compares the trailing bytes to the active nonce. The [official release record](https://github.com/node-opcua/node-opcua/releases) describes 2.166.0 as adding nonce verification to protect username credentials from replay. The scanner therefore accepts exact affected builds through 2.165.2 and treats 2.166.0 as the first repaired release.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add `node-opcua-server-username-token-nonce-bypass` with synthetic network source `untrusted-opcua-username-identity-token` at the actual `start()` call, construction sink `vulnerable-node-opcua-username-token-missing-nonce-binding`, CWE-347, and exact runtime provenance. Reuse the established official-binding and stable-instance discipline for named/aliased ESM, namespace imports, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS receivers, destructures, direct members, same-file startup, and an exported instance started through a relative import. Additionally require a constructor option that resolves to a usable user manager: an inline or referenced object must expose `isValidUser`, while imported/member and factory-produced managers are retained for reviewer confirmation. The package's absent manager is deny-all and cannot be exploited, so omitted, null, empty, primitive, and certificate-only managers are negative. Default endpoint policy includes encrypted username tokens. An explicit literal `SecurityPolicy.None`-only configuration does not, and is rejected; a dynamic policy list whose contents cannot be proven also fails closed. Explicit endpoint arrays are inspected independently so a top-level default is not incorrectly credited when every configured endpoint is None-only. Existing exact production declaration and fresh declaration-consistent npm lock/shrinkwrap v2/v3 rules apply. Repaired or unproved versions, development-only and wrong packages, unresolved ranges, invalid precedence, reassigned bindings or instances, replaced members, wrapper shadows, client-only or unstarted code, local lookalikes, and test/example paths stay negative.

**Executable witness and impact separation.** Source-identical fixtures pin the aggregate and transitive server to 2.165.2 and 2.166.0 with complete locks. Their witness uses the package's real protected authentication method, an ephemeral 2,048-bit RSA key, `SecurityPolicy.Basic256Sha256`, and two distinct 32-byte session nonces without opening a listener. It encrypts `correct horse || nonceA` once. Version 2.165.2 accepts the ciphertext under nonce A, accepts the identical ciphertext again under nonce B, and calls the user manager twice with the same password. Version 2.166.0 accepts nonce A but rejects nonce B before the second manager call. A second four-byte plaintext declares a length equal to the nonce length while containing neither password nor nonce. The affected build derives an empty password and reaches the deliberately empty-password-compatible test manager; the repaired build rejects it before the manager. Reviewer guidance keeps these effects separate: replay applies to any credential accepted by the configured manager, while an empty-password authentication bypass exists only if that manager demonstrably accepts empty credentials. Neither result establishes post-login authorization failure, execution, disclosure, or industrial-process manipulation without additional evidence.

**Initial regression evidence.** Eight focused groups pass 53 assertions across official binding shapes, exact 2.165.0/1/2 and repaired 2.166.0 boundaries, manager and policy negatives, cross-file startup, dependency proof, reassignment/replacement/shadowing barriers, source identity, strict manifest gates, and prompt guidance. The adjacent node-opcua plus canonical benchmark lane passes 31 tests and 1,655 assertions. Windows Node and Ubuntu/WSL Node both reproduce `sessionA:true`, `replayedAcrossSessions:true`, `forgedEmptyPassword:true`, and three manager calls on 2.165.2; both return true/false/false with one manager call on 2.166.0. The perfect-gate pair advances the benchmark to 89 exploit/control pairs, 178 cases, and 534 three-run scans. Full scanner, package, desktop, self-review, and hosted acceptance follow the implementation checkpoint.

## 2026-08-24 — Require a started node-opcua server before reporting its unbounded nonce cache

**Candidate selection and coverage gap.** Recent high-impact npm advisories offered several plausible increments. The PDF.js scripting issue depends on a browser renderer, default-enabled scripting, attacker-controlled PDF loading, and the absence of a blocking CSP; an application model that stops at `getDocument` would overstate reachability. The Unleash issue is primarily a deployed product-version condition whose realistic witness requires the server's database-backed runtime. [GHSA-6wvw-vrw4-363w / CVE-2026-54156](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6wvw-vrw4-363w) instead has a narrow application boundary: code imports the official aggregate `node-opcua` package, constructs `OPCUAServer`, and starts that instance. Current official CodeQL and public Semgrep rule-source searches found no node-opcua nonce-cache model. This is an inferred model gap, not evidence that dependency inventory products miss the vulnerable package; the value is distinguishing a reachable server from client-only or unused dependency presence.

**Repair semantics and version discipline.** The reviewed GitHub range is exactly `node-opcua <=2.165.0`; do not broaden it merely because 2.168.0 is the cited repair release. The published 2.165.0 aggregate resolves `node-opcua-secure-channel` 2.165.0, whose `server_secure_channel_layer` stores every nonempty base64 nonce in a process-global object and never removes an entry. The published 2.168.0 aggregate resolves the matching repaired secure-channel package, which moves nonce tracking into a timestamped `Map`, lazily removes entries older than four hours, and drops the oldest entries above 50,000. Versions 2.165.1 through 2.167.x lie between the reviewed affected endpoint and cited repair release; they remain negative unless independent primary evidence proves that a particular release still contains the flaw. Exact production declarations or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock/shrinkwrap evidence are accepted; ranges without a usable lock, development-only declarations, v1 or inconsistent locks, and an invalid higher-precedence shrinkwrap fail closed.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add `node-opcua-server-nonce-cache-dos` with synthetic network source `untrusted-opcua-session-nonce` at the actual `start()` call, construction sink `vulnerable-node-opcua-unbounded-nonce-cache-dos`, CWE-770 plus demonstrated CWE-400, and exact dependency provenance. Resolve named and aliased ESM, namespace, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS receiver, destructure, and direct-member bindings. Require the same non-reassigned constructed instance to reach `start`; preserve the common cross-file topology where an exported server instance is imported relatively and started by a bootstrap module. Reject `OPCUAClient`-only code, construction without startup, wrong packages, local lookalikes, reassigned bindings or instances, replaced `OPCUAServer` or `start` members, wrapper parameter shadows, and test/example paths. `maxSessions`, authentication configuration, and normal session expiry are not credited as cache bounds because the vulnerable store is process-global and retains entries after session teardown. Reviewer guidance limits claims to resource allocation and demonstrated availability impact; nonce retention alone does not establish authentication bypass, message execution, disclosure, or industrial-process manipulation.

**Bounded witness and regression evidence.** Add source-identical `node-opcua` 2.165.0 and 2.168.0 fixtures with complete exact npm locks and a perfect-gate specialized manifest. The witness calls the package's real server nonce-tracking function with 50,001 unique nonempty 32-byte values, then replays the first. The affected build returns `firstNonceRetained: true`; the repaired build returns false because the size ceiling evicted it. Windows Node and Ubuntu/WSL Node reproduce both outcomes without opening a listener or deliberately consuming unbounded memory. Seven focused groups pass 59 assertions across official bindings, the exact reviewed boundary, exported-instance cross-file startup, lock precedence, negative controls, pair identity, and guidance. The widened Windows lane passes 117 tests and 1,439 assertions with one expected symlink skip; Ubuntu/WSL passes 26 focused tests and 230 assertions. The pair advances the canonical benchmark to 88 exploit/control pairs, 176 cases, and 528 three-run scans.

**Final scanner and package acceptance.** Exact implementation checkpoint `05ad9dc9ac3b4428e2bacd9542120c8a40109b9d` passes the authoritative Bun 1.3.14 suite with 1,373 tests, 10,484 assertions, 20 intentional environment/platform skips, zero failures, and a 324.65-second runtime across 153 files. ## 2026-08-24 — Separate nanoid's negative-size and zero-default infinite loops

**Trigger and repair boundaries.** Two reviewed advisories cover related but non-interchangeable generator failures. [GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv / CVE-2026-67214](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv) reaches `nanoid/non-secure`'s decrement loop with a negative size; decrementing a negative integer never reaches falsy zero. The repaired boundaries are 3.3.16 and 5.1.16, with every 4.x release affected. [GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 / CVE-2026-67213](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8) reaches a main-package custom generator whose factory default makes its random-work step zero; the returned generator's unconditional loop cannot accumulate output. The Node entry is repaired at 3.3.17 and 5.1.6. The later 3.3.18 change is specific to the React Native asynchronous file and is not used as the Node boundary. Current official rule-source searches find no `nanoid` model, so dependency alerts alone cannot decide whether attacker input reaches either exact API and argument position.

**Executable semantics before pattern matching.** An isolated exact-version matrix rejected several tempting generalizations. `nanoid/non-secure` 3.3.15 and 5.1.15 hang for `nanoid(-1)`, while 3.3.16 and 5.1.16 return an empty string. Official npm archive manifests establish that 1.x/2.x expose `non-secure` as a callable CommonJS/default surface, whereas 3.x introduces the named exports used by later releases; the model accepts each major's real shape and rejects impossible cross-major calls. Main `customAlphabet("abc", 0)()` hangs on 3.3.16 and 5.1.5 but returns normally on 3.3.17 and 5.1.6. Conversely, `customAlphabet("abc")(0)` on 5.1.5 returns one character: a zero per-call argument is not the reviewed zero factory-default condition. A factory configured from remote input is also safe for this cause when the generator is called with a positive override. The model consequently represents factory construction and returned-generator invocation as two linked operations, recognizes omitted and explicit `undefined` default use, and declines an assigned or immediate factory that is never invoked or whose default is overridden.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add one `node-http-nanoid-size-dos` model with cause-specific sink kinds and exact version predicates. Resolve named aliases, namespace receivers, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS receivers/destructures/direct members, assigned factories, and immediate ESM/CommonJS factory calls. `nanoid/non-secure` accepts remote negative-size reachability through direct `nanoid`, the generator's call argument, or a used factory default. The main package accepts only a remote custom-generator factory default followed by an invocation that actually uses it; main-package `nanoid(remote)` and generator-only `customAlphabet("abc")(remote)` remain negative. Require nearest exact production metadata or fresh declaration-consistent npm lock/shrinkwrap v2/v3 evidence. Fail closed on repaired, wrong, development-only, unresolved, stale, legacy, or precedence-invalid metadata; fixed input; test/example paths; reassignment or member replacement; wrapper shadows; and uninvoked or replaced generators. A pre-sink negative guard receives credit only when it terminates the path. The zero-default cause requires a terminating `!Number.isInteger(size) || size <= 0`-equivalent proof; a lower bound alone does not exclude `NaN`, which can also collapse the work step. Retain CWE-835 and CWE-400 without inferring execution, data disclosure, or authorization failure from event-loop occupation.

**Benchmark and initial evidence.** Add source-identical four-file fixtures pinned to exact `nanoid` 5.1.15 and 5.1.16. Both carry `request.query.size` from `src/server.mjs:4` through gateway and service wrappers to `nanoid/non-secure.nanoid` at `src/storage.mjs:4`; only the affected version emits the specialized row and exact runtime-dependency provenance. A kill-bounded child-process witness makes the positive's nontermination testable without hanging the suite and requires the repaired twin to exit with the JSON empty string. Windows Node and clean Ubuntu/WSL Node reproduce timeout plus `SIGKILL` for 5.1.15 and normal exit for 5.1.16. Ten focused groups cover legacy callable/default and modern named bindings, direct and custom generators, immediate CommonJS factories, both cause boundaries, factory-default overrides, exact and lock proof, npm v2/v3 and shrinkwrap precedence, reassignments, replacement, shadowing, test paths, strong guards, typed cross-file propagation, pair identity, strict manifest gates, and reviewer guidance; they pass 92 assertions. The widened Windows lane passes 114 tests and 2,882 assertions with one expected host-specific skip, while clean WSL passes 33 tests and 1,678 assertions. Formatting, generated-model drift, and TypeScript compilation pass. The new perfect-gate pair advances the canonical benchmark to 87 exploit/control pairs, 174 cases, and 522 three-run scans. Both generated fixture installs and the isolated version-research directory are removed before commit. Full scanner, compiled self-review, package, desktop, and hosted acceptance follow the pushed implementation checkpoint.

## 2026-08-23 — Resolve Socket.IO server parser risk through the installed dependency graph

**Why the direct parser model is insufficient.** Ordinary Socket.IO applications do not import `socket.io-parser`; they instantiate or call the public `socket.io` server, which creates one Decoder per Engine.IO client and passes every incoming Engine.IO data message to `decoder.add`. The [official server client implementation](https://github.com/socketio/socket.io/blob/main/packages/socket.io/lib/client.ts) catches parser exceptions and closes the connection, but an affected parser accepts the impossible zero-attachment packet and therefore never reaches that error path. The [protocol specification](https://github.com/socketio/socket.io/blob/main/docs/socket.io-protocol/v5-current.md) also makes the wire boundary explicit: Engine.IO message type `4` prefixes the Socket.IO binary-event packet `50-["evt"]`, producing `450-["evt"]` on the WebSocket. Application event callbacks occur after this parser state transition, so callback-level validation cannot prevent it.

**Dependency decision.** A `socket.io` release is not enough evidence to infer the parser repair. Current 4.8.x packages declare `socket.io-parser: ~4.2.4`, so an older lock can retain 4.2.6 while a newly resolved lock selects 4.2.7 for the same parent and application source. Add a declaration-consistent transitive lock resolver rather than mapping parent versions to guessed child versions. It requires a nearest direct production declaration, npm lockfile or shrinkwrap format 2/3, an identical root declaration, the matching installed parent, the parent's literal child declaration, and either its nested child or the root-hoisted child satisfying the supported exact/tilde/caret range. `npm-shrinkwrap.json` has precedence; an invalid higher-precedence shrinkwrap fails closed instead of falling back to `package-lock.json`. This narrow helper intentionally does not claim Yarn Plug'n'Play, pnpm virtual-store graphs, aliases, workspaces, tags, Git dependencies, or arbitrary semver grammar.

**Reachability and precision contract.** Add `node-socketio-server-transitive-parser-dos` only for an official `socket.io` Server constructor or supported callable export that produces a retained instance and is exposed through a numeric port or an attached HTTP server proven to call `listen`. Resolve named and aliased imports, namespace receivers, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS receivers, destructures, direct `.Server` members, bound callable exports, and inline `require("socket.io")(...)`; the callable shape retains coverage for the 2.x line whose dependency can select parser 3.4.4. Require default parser selection. A literal spread-free options object without `parser` is acceptable, while a custom parser, computed property, spread, or dynamic options value is ambiguous and rejected. Also reject non-listening attachment targets, unexposed instances, wrong or development-only packages, missing/v1/stale/inconsistent locks, a child outside the parent's declaration, repaired child branches, binding, instance, or attachment-target reassignment, replaced `Server` or `_parser` members, and test/example paths. Record the Server construction or callable initialization as the sink, the concrete network-listening line as the source, and separate parent and child dependency propagators. Retain CWE-400/CWE-20/CWE-754 without inflating the state defect into event execution, authorization bypass, prototype pollution, or network compromise.

**Executable benchmark and regression evidence.** Add source- and parent-identical `socket.io@4.8.3` fixtures with real npm locks; only the `socket.io-parser` lock entry changes from 4.2.6 to 4.2.7. Both locks pass `npm ci`, and the parent's unchanged `~4.2.4` declaration selects each child legitimately. A loopback-only witness opens a real Engine.IO WebSocket, completes the namespace connection, sends `450-["evt"]`, and then sends at most 512 distinct 4 KiB binary frames. Windows Node 24.15.0 and Ubuntu/WSL Node 22.23.1 both measure 512 retained frames and 2,097,152 retained bytes on 4.2.6; 4.2.7 retains zero and the server's caught parser error closes the client. Direct regressions cover constructors and callables, 3.4.4/3.4.5 and 4.2.6/4.2.7 boundaries, npm v2/v3, shrinkwrap precedence, nested installs, parser-option ambiguity, listener reachability, graph inconsistencies, replacement, test paths, exact provenance, fixture identity, perfect-gate metadata, and reviewer guidance. The widened Windows lane passes 121 tests and 2,891 assertions with one intentional POSIX-symlink skip; Ubuntu/WSL passes all 122 tests and 2,892 assertions. The exact implementation commit's authoritative Bun 1.3.14 suite passes 1,356 tests and 10,311 assertions across 151 files with 20 intentional environment/platform skips, zero failures, and a 305.83-second runtime. The strict pair advances the canonical corpus to 86 exploit/control pairs, 172 cases, and 516 three-run scans. Generated fixture installs and the isolated research tree are removed before commit.

**Final scanner and package acceptance.** Exact implementation checkpoint `1f6acfffd31965a204ea2dc406fb705951361cf1` passes generated-model drift, formatting, TypeScript compilation, a clean production build, and `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high`. Two compiled inventories of an isolated exact-HEAD archive take 25,386.308 and 10,870.209 ms and produce 96 byte-identical records, 237,264 bytes, and SHA-256 `446c16ebb95e166f4354c195cfba34e115aa2a0efd1619955418cdd24255dfdf`; 92 records are benchmark-fixture paths. It carries network source `src/server.mjs:6`, Server-construction sink `src/server.mjs:5`, CWE-400/CWE-20/CWE-754, `socket.io@4.8.3:manifest-exact:server-network-parser-exposure`, and `socket.io-parser@4.2.6:npm-lockfile:~4.2.4:zero-attachment-buffer-retention`. The source- and parent-identical 4.2.7 fixture emits no specialized row. The archive and staging directory are removed.

## 2026-08-23 — Require persistent Socket.IO decoder state for zero-attachment retention

**Trigger and comparative coverage.** The reviewed high-severity [GHSA-2m8v-j782-fhvr / CVE-2026-69185](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2m8v-j782-fhvr) affects `socket.io-parser` below 3.3.6, from 3.4.0 below 3.4.5, and from 4.0.0 below 4.2.7. A binary event or acknowledgement that declares zero attachments is accepted and emitted while its `BinaryReconstructor` remains live. Each later binary frame is pushed before the equality check, so a positive buffer length can never equal zero and the persistent connection retains attacker-selected memory until parser teardown. The three upstream repair commits reject attachment counts below one. Authenticated current-source searches find no `socket.io-parser` or `maxAttachments` reference in official CodeQL. CodeQL's seven Socket.IO references model server/client event sources and objects after parsing, not this pre-callback state invariant. Current public Semgrep rules and the reviewed reference scanner contain no matching model.

**Executable repair boundary.** An isolated alias matrix exercises 3.3.5/3.3.6, 3.4.4/3.4.5, and 4.2.6/4.2.7 through their real `Decoder` APIs. On each affected release, `50-["evt"]` emits once, leaves a reconstructor, accepts 128 following 4 KiB buffers, and retains all 128. Each repaired twin raises `Illegal attachments` on the initial string, emits nothing, retains no reconstructor, and accepts no later frame in the witness. The accepted package-backed fixture widens the bounded sample to 2,048 distinct 4 KiB frames: both Windows Node 24.15.0 and Ubuntu/WSL Node 22.23.1 measure 8,388,608 retained bytes on 4.2.6 and zero on 4.2.7. This is a state and lifetime boundary, not a throughput comparison.

**Precision contract.** Add `node-http-socketio-parser-zero-attachment-dos` only when the nearest production dependency is exact or a fresh declaration-consistent npm lockfile v2/v3 resolution, the proven version belongs to an affected branch, and an official non-reassigned Decoder constructs a module-scope persistent instance whose unmodified `add` method receives remote input. Resolve named/aliased imports, namespace and interoperable default receivers, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS receivers/destructures/direct members, but reject Encoder, fixed packets, wrong or development-only packages, unresolved ranges, stale/inconsistent/v1 locks, replaced Decoder or `add` members, identifier reassignment, wrapper shadows, tests/examples, and decoders constructed inside a handler or nested block. The lifetime requirement deliberately declines package-only and request-local hypotheses: later binary frames must reach the same retained reconstructor. `maxAttachments` is not control evidence because the invalid zero value bypasses the intended positive-count invariant, and the advisory identifies upgrade as the supported remedy. Retain CWE-400 plus the advisory's CWE-20/CWE-754 without inflating the parser state flaw into execution or authorization bypass.

**Benchmark and initial evidence.** Add topology-identical four-file 4.2.6/4.2.7 fixtures. Both carry `request.body` from `src/server.js:7` through gateway and service wrappers to the module-scope decoder at `src/storage.js:6`; only 4.2.6 emits the specialized row and exact `socket.io-parser@4.2.6:manifest-exact:zero-attachment-buffer-retention` provenance. Their production sources and bounded witnesses are byte-identical, while only the exact package pin differs. The specialized manifest requires high severity, CWE-400/CWE-20/CWE-754, validation, attack path, code evidence, perfect precision/recall, and zero false positives. ## 2026-08-23 — Correlate Nodemailer raw content with its disclosure recipient

**Trigger and comparative coverage.** The reviewed high-severity [GHSA-p6gq-j5cr-w38f](https://github.com/nodemailer/nodemailer/security/advisories/GHSA-p6gq-j5cr-w38f) shows that Nodemailer through 9.0.0 creates the message-level `raw` root MIME node without forwarding `disableFileAccess` or `disableUrlAccess`. Consequently, `{path}` and `{href}` raw values are resolved despite the application's explicit deny policy and their bytes become the delivered message. The [9.0.1 repair](https://github.com/nodemailer/nodemailer/commit/a82e060) passes both flags to that root node. Official CodeQL's `EmailClients.qll` recognizes `createTransport().sendMail()` but exposes only text, HTML, recipient, sender, and subject; authenticated current-source search finds no `disableFileAccess` reference. Current public Semgrep rules and the reference scanner contain no Nodemailer model. This is an application reachability gap, not a reason to turn every vulnerable dependency declaration into a finding.

**Executable repair boundary.** Safely removed installs under Windows Node 24.15.0 and Ubuntu/WSL Node 22.23.1 reproduce the same result. With identical stream transport and both deny flags, 9.0.0 places a benign temporary-file sentinel into the message for `raw:{path}` and a loopback-only HTTP response sentinel into the message for `raw:{href}`. Its ordinary attachment control over the same file fails with `EFILEACCESS`, proving the policy exists and isolating the raw-root omission. Version 9.0.1 rejects the raw cases with `EFILEACCESS` and `EURLACCESS`. This also establishes the effect split: file policy proves a CWE-73/CWE-200 candidate, URL policy proves a CWE-918/CWE-200 candidate, and neither implies the other when only one flag is configured.

Resolve official default, namespace, TypeScript import-equals, named/destructured, CommonJS receiver/direct-member, and inline-require `createTransport` forms; reject identifier or member reassignment and transporter or `sendMail` replacement. Require a literal true deny flag on the resolved spread-free transport options or spread-free message, then exact message-level `raw` at `sendMail`. The first fixture carried raw content and recipient as two parameters. Although both originated at one route, the existing path record proved only the raw branch and merely observed the second sink parameter. That form was rejected as insufficiently correlated. The accepted source-identical pair carries one complete request-controlled message object through all three wrappers, and both `raw` and `to` must reference that same proven wrapper parameter. Split parameters remain negative until a second correlated path can be represented explicitly. Fixed raw data or recipient, ordinary content nodes, replaceable spreads, patched/development/wrong/unresolved metadata, stale/v1 locks, lookalikes, non-sendMail methods, and tests/examples fail closed.

## 2026-08-23 — Bind fast-uri encoded dot segments to a protected filesystem effect

**Trigger and comparative coverage.** The reviewed high-severity [GHSA-q3j6-qgpj-74h6 / CVE-2026-6321](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/security/advisories/GHSA-q3j6-qgpj-74h6) identifies a distinct path-policy flaw in `fast-uri`: releases through 2.4.0 and 3.0.0 through 3.1.0 decode percent-encoded separators and dot segments before dot-segment removal in `normalize()` and `equal()`. A URI that lexically appears under `/public/` can therefore collapse to `/admin/`. Versions 2.4.1 and 3.1.1 preserve reserved path escapes as data; the [upstream repair](https://github.com/fastify/fast-uri/commit/876ce79b662c3e5015e4e7dffe6f37752ad34f35) adds explicit parse, normalize, and equality regressions for `%2F` and `%2E`. The existing host-policy model deliberately mentions but does not report this advisory because a parser-versus-network-host disagreement proves SSRF, while this issue requires a protected-path effect. Current official CodeQL and Semgrep source searches contain no `fast-uri` package or advisory model; a reviewed reference scanner has no corresponding application model.

**Executable boundary and rejected witness.** Safely removed isolated installs of 2.4.0, 2.4.1, 3.1.0, and 3.1.1 process the exact URI `https://assets.example/public/%2e%2e/admin/config.json`. The affected releases normalize and parse it as `/admin/config.json`; the repaired releases retain `/public/%2E%2E/admin/config.json`. A rooted Node path therefore changes from `asset-store/admin/config.json` to the literal in-policy target `asset-store/public/%2E%2E/admin/config.json`, and vulnerable `equal()` alone equates the hostile URI with the protected canonical URI while repaired releases do not. The first candidate application parsed the repaired normalized URI with WHATWG `new URL()`. Runtime testing showed that WHATWG correctly treats the retained encoded parent as URL syntax and collapses it again, leaving both dependency versions unsafe. That candidate was rejected rather than laundering an unrelated consumer mismatch into a version-only control. The accepted witness keeps the second parse inside repaired `fast-uri`, then supplies its preserved path data directly to the filesystem construction.

**Precision contract.** Add `node-path-fast-uri-encoded-dot-segment-policy-bypass` only as a specialization of an existing `node-http-path` record, preserving its exact remote source, cross-file wrappers, official Node filesystem sink, and CWE-22. Require nearest exact production metadata or a fresh declaration-consistent npm lockfile v2/v3 resolution in an affected branch. In the sink wrapper, the same remote parameter must pass a pre-sink fail-closed negated `startsWith` decision against a fixed canonical HTTP(S) URL whose path is a non-root subtree ending in `/`. The sink path must be an exact official, non-reassigned `node:path` `join` or `resolve` rooted by a fixed server string, and a later argument must contain exact official, non-reassigned `fast-uri.parse(fast-uri.normalize(remote)).path`. Named or aliased imports, default/namespace receivers, TypeScript import-equals, and CommonJS destructures or receivers are eligible through the shared binding parser. Repaired versions, package-only evidence, development-only or wrong packages, unresolved ranges, stale or v1 locks, noncanonical/root-only prefixes, positive, mismatched, log-only, post-sink, or conditionally non-terminal decisions, missing normalize or parse-path stages, WHATWG reparsing, unrooted paths, fixed inputs, reassigned or shadowed bindings, local lookalikes, and tests/examples fail closed.

**Impact and reviewer boundary.** The broken raw-prefix decision is recorded as candidate control evidence, not called a sanitizer. Final review must reproduce the exact installed release and spelling, show the `fast-uri` normalized and parsed paths, show the actual filesystem path after every later decode or platform conversion, and identify the protected sibling or parent resource reached. It must separately account for alternate separators, Windows drive and volume syntax, case folding, symbolic and hard links, junctions, mounts, attacker-writable ancestors, rename races, process permissions, tenant/object authorization, and the concrete read, disclosure, create, overwrite, delete, move, metadata, or served-content effect. The row does not establish SSRF, arbitrary filesystem reach, execution, persistence, or privilege escalation without that evidence. Conversely, upgrading `fast-uri` does not make a later WHATWG or percent-decoding consumer safe if that consumer deliberately converts the preserved escape back into live path syntax.
