## 2026-08-23 — Model ip-address decimal/octal disagreement as a broken SSRF control

**Trigger and comparative coverage.** The reviewed high-severity [GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr / CVE-2026-69192](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mwp4-54f8-5fhr) affects `ip-address` through 10.3.0. Its IPv4 parser accepts multi-digit octets beginning with zero and interprets them as decimal, while WHATWG URL and common native resolver paths can preserve historical octal meaning. An application can therefore parse and classify `012.0.0.1` as public `12.0.0.1`, allow it through a fail-closed private-range guard, and send the original spelling to private `10.0.0.1`. The [10.3.1 repair](https://github.com/beaugunderson/ip-address/commit/56368cb3d66c73ba0ee9b6b834fd31b22c2fd71e) rejects every multi-digit leading-zero octet before normalization. Searches of current official CodeQL source find no `Address4` model and only unrelated text matches for `ip-address`; current official Semgrep rules likewise contain no `Address4` coverage and only unrelated public-IP identifiers. A reviewed reference scanner has no `ip-address` or `Address4` application model. Generic SSRF dataflow can retain the source and sink, but it treats the fail-closed address check as candidate validation and cannot determine that two consumers disagree about the exact spelling.

**Executable API and network boundary.** Safely removed isolated package aliases establish that the public package begins at 3.2.0; 3.2.0 and 4.2.0 export the legacy `v4.Address` constructor and `isInSubnet`, while 5.x and later expose named `Address4`. Modern `isPrivate`, `isLoopback`, `isLinkLocal`, and `isCGNAT` classifiers first appear in 10.2.0, and `isHostInSubnet` follows in 10.2.2. Version 10.3.0 accepts `012.0.0.1` and returns `12.0.0.1` from `correctForm`; 10.3.1 throws. Node's WHATWG URL implementation maps the same spelling to `10.0.0.1`. Native Ubuntu `getent ahostsv4` independently resolves `012.0.0.1` to `10.0.0.1`, `012.012.012.012` to `10.10.10.10`, and `010.0.0.1` to `8.0.0.1`. Windows native resolution did not accept this spelling in the tested path, so reviewer guidance requires proof for the deployed URL parser, resolver, proxy, client, operating system, and network stack instead of assuming universal reachability.

**Precision contract.** Add `node-ssrf-ip-address-leading-zero-guard-bypass` as a specialization of a proven `node-http-ssrf` row rather than a package-presence alert. Require nearest exact production evidence or a fresh declaration-consistent npm lockfile v2/v3 resolution from 3.2.0 through 10.3.0. Require an exact named, aliased, destructured, namespace, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS receiver, or legacy `v4.Address` binding from `ip-address`; reject default imports and similarly named packages. Tie the constructor argument to the same host or hostname derived from the outbound value, require a pre-sink fail-closed classifier, and preserve the original outbound expression. Accept modern classifiers only from 10.2.0. On older APIs, require the concrete `isInSubnet` range `10.0.0.0/8`, because that is the private destination established by the reviewed leading-zero witness. Reject 10.3.1+, pre-publication 3.0/3.1 guesses, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent or v1 locks, development-only metadata, repaired lock resolutions, wrong packages, reassigned bindings, log-only decisions, another checked value, tests/examples, and an earlier fail-closed `^0\d` check only when that rejection references the exact host. Emit CWE-918 with CWE-20 context. Patching the parser disagreement does not replace redirect checks, connection-time A/AAAA validation or pinning, DNS-rebinding defense, proxy review, and complete reserved-range policy.

**Benchmark and acceptance boundary.** Add source-identical four-file fixtures pinned to 10.3.0 and 10.3.1. Both carry `request.query.url` from `src/server.js:7` through gateway and service wrappers into `src/storage.js`, classify the exact derived host at line 6, and call `fetch` with the original value at line 7; only the affected dependency emits the specialized row. The positive retains ten relative-import, wrapper-call, wrapper-parameter, and runtime-dependency propagators. Bounded dependency-free witnesses prove the decimal/octal interpretation split and repaired leading-zero rejection without requiring vulnerable packages during routine tests. Eight direct groups cover modern, CommonJS, and legacy bindings; the 3.2.0 and 10.2.0 API boundaries; exact and lock-resolved dependency proof; repaired, wrong, development-only, range-only, default-import, reassigned, log-only, wrong-value, and test-path negatives; exact versus unrelated leading-zero checks; cross-file topology; reviewer guidance; and perfect specialized thresholds. The pair advances the canonical corpus to 80 exploit/control pairs and 480 repeated scans. Windows and native Ubuntu/WSL focused lanes each pass 44 tests and 1,572 assertions. Formatting, generated output, TypeScript, the clean build, both witnesses, and `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` are green. The authoritative Windows suite passes 1,311 tests and 9,892 assertions across 145 files with 20 intentional skips and zero failures in 299.55 seconds.

## 2026-08-23 — Close the legacy js-yaml ordered-map repair gap

**Trigger and comparative coverage.** The reviewed high-severity [GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5p4m-2wfm-xmqj) identifies a separate quadratic parser path that the first js-yaml model increment incorrectly treated as repaired. In the default 3.x/4.x schema, `resolveYamlOmap()` checks each unique `!!omap` key with `objectKeys.indexOf()`, so an `n`-entry sequence performs `1 + 2 + ... + n` comparisons synchronously. The 10,000 total-merge-key limit in 3.15.0/4.3.0 never reaches this resolver and therefore closes only the `<<` alias-chain path. The official 3.15.1 and 4.3.1 backports replace the growing array with an own-property dictionary ([3.x repair](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/commit/22a8071ef032117bc6249c330b240ac3aa2d3ded), [4.x repair](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/commit/c3cc4b0bb9ddb9af2dd9b61e0d56f5ce7983cd4a)). The analogous YAML 1.1-schema defect affects 5.0.0 through 5.2.0 and was independently repaired in 5.2.1 ([CVE-2026-59870 repair](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/commit/39f3211a2f01b3c6982710cf21434ab7060acefe)). Authenticated searches of current official CodeQL and Semgrep rule sources return zero `resolveYamlOmap`, `omapTag`, and `YAML11_SCHEMA` references. Historical unsafe-deserialization classification does not express this availability mechanism or the two legacy repair boundaries.

**Executable boundary validation.** A safely removed npm-alias matrix ran exact 3.15.0, 3.15.1, 4.3.0, and 4.3.1 packages under Node 24.15.0 with identical default-schema documents. At 10,000 entries and 157,787 bytes, the four runs took 71.505, 35.135, 75.813, and 43.940 ms. At 20,000 entries and 337,787 bytes they took 288.409, 51.759, 312.451, and 50.297 ms. At 40,000 entries and 697,787 bytes they took 1,398.628, 76.870, 1,402.917, and 89.273 ms. Doubling the largest affected input therefore multiplies work by about 4.5, while the repaired implementations remain close to parser-linear scaling. Every parse returned the expected 40,000-element ordered map; the timing is resolver work rather than an exception path. The temporary packages were removed after validation.

Older 3.x/4.x releases remain `quadratic-merge` candidates because the same remote loader call already proves an independently reachable default-schema stall; 5.0.0 through 5.2.0 remain `exponential-flow` candidates because that stronger sub-200-byte path covers every overlapping omap-affected release, and 5.2.1 remains flow-pair-only. This precedence eliminates the two false-negative versions without emitting duplicate rows for a single sink. Keep load/loadAll on 3.x/4.x and safeLoad/safeLoadAll on 3.x, exact package and production proof, remote argument-zero flow, reassignment and shadow rejection, and CWE-400/CWE-407 availability scope. Reviewer guidance must establish a default-schema `!!omap` sequence, unique-key count, input bytes, duplicate-key lookup behavior, runtime scaling, event-loop impact, and practical request-size acceptance. Merge-key caps, depth limits, body limits larger than the demonstrated document, and ordinary exception handling do not preempt this synchronous work.

**Focused evidence.** Add topology-identical four-file 4.3.0/4.3.1 fixtures with source `src/server.js:7`, sink `src/storage.js:4`, and nine ordered relative-import/call/parameter propagators. The vulnerable witness counts exactly `n(n-1)/2` comparisons over 4,000 unique keys; the repaired witness proves one own-key lookup per entry. ## 2026-08-23 — Separate js-yaml parser complexity from unsafe deserialization

**Trigger and comparative coverage.** Two reviewed 2026 advisories describe independent synchronous parser-complexity defects in the exact same npm package. GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m / CVE-2026-59869 affects `js-yaml` 3.0.0 through 3.14.x and 4.0.0 through 4.2.x: each mapping that merges its predecessor enumerates an increasing inherited-key set, producing quadratic work from linear input. Releases 3.15.0 and 4.3.0 add a default 10,000 total-merge-key limit ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m), [official 4.x repair](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/commit/59423c6)). GHSA-pm4m-ph32-ghv5 / CVE-2026-73643 affects the rewritten 5.0.0 through 5.2.1 parser: a nested flow-sequence entry later recognized as a key/value pair is restored and parsed a second time at every level, yielding exponential work and minute-scale blocking from fewer than 200 bytes. Version 5.2.2 inserts mapping events around the already parsed key instead ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pm4m-ph32-ghv5), [official repair](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml/commit/3e5240f)). Authenticated searches of current official sources return zero `js-yaml` and zero `maxTotalMergeKeys` references in Semgrep's public rules. CodeQL has seven `js-yaml` references, all in the historical CWE-502 unsafe-deserialization customization, examples, help, tests, and changelog; it has no `maxTotalMergeKeys` reference and treats `safeLoad` as the deserialization control. That makes the quadratic 3.x `safeLoad` path a concrete false negative for the existing semantic category, while ordinary `load` findings risk being mislabeled as code execution rather than availability loss.

The comparison deliberately records runtime, payload bytes, depth, outcome, and exact installed version rather than extrapolating from package presence. Reject pre-3 releases, 3.15.0, 4.3.0, 5.2.2 and later, fixed input, unavailable methods, wrong or development-only packages, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, reassignment, and wrapper shadowing. Do not credit `maxDepth: 100` for the 5.x defect: practical denial occurs around 30 to 40 levels. Request body limits do not control a sub-200-byte payload, and ordinary `try/catch` cannot preempt synchronous CPU work. Report CWE-400/CWE-407 availability only; historical executable tags, prototype pollution, alias memory expansion, and code execution are separate contracts.

## 2026-08-23 — Distinguish node-tar member-filter recursion from decompression volume

**Trigger and scanner comparison.** Reviewed GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m / CVE-2026-73566 describes uncontrolled recursion in node-tar's internal `filesFilter/mapHas` helper through 7.5.20. `t/list` or `x/extract` installs this filter only when the consumer supplies a non-empty member-selection list. A GNU `L` or PAX `x` header can carry tens of thousands of slash-separated segments within the existing 1 MiB metadata cap. The parser calls the filter before emitting the entry, so extraction's later `maxDepth` check cannot run; `t/list` has no such check. On asynchronous file and stream consumers the resulting `RangeError` escapes the awaited promise and terminates the process. The official 7.5.21 repair adds a 100-level recursion bound to `mapHas` ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-r292-9mhp-454m), [official repair `631ae59`](https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar/commit/631ae59121bf8fc8a22bbae35f074cb9b789cd4a), [7.5.21 release](https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar/releases/tag/v7.5.21)). Authenticated official source searches find no node-tar rule in Semgrep. CodeQL has an experimental decompression-bomb model for `x/extract`, but it treats decompressed bytes and `maxReadSize` as its boundary; it does not include `t/list`, member selection, installed version, or the pre-entry recursive filter.

**Model decision and precision boundary.** Add a separate `node-http-tar-member-selection-recursion` identity with CWE-674 rather than widening the linkpath-traversal model or the generic decompression signal. Accept official namespace/default and TypeScript import-equals receivers, named or aliased `t`/`list`/`x`/`extract` functions, CommonJS receivers/destructures, and direct require members. Require nearest exact production metadata or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 resolution through 7.5.20, attacker-controlled archive flow through options `file` or the request stream, and a non-empty member list. Reject 7.5.21+, fixed archives, omitted/empty lists, create APIs, exact `sync: true`, wrong or development-only packages, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, reassignment, and wrapper shadowing. Do not credit `maxDepth`, `maxReadSize`, or ordinary `try/catch`: they address later entry depth, byte volume, or promise rejection rather than the reviewed filter exception. Synchronous execution is excluded from this process-termination model because its `RangeError` is catchable.

**Impact and benchmark contract.** Final review must establish an accepted GNU long-name or PAX path header, metadata body size, effective slash-segment count after header parsing, non-empty consumer member selection, asynchronous or stream execution, runtime stack limit, the filter call before entry guards, an uncaught `RangeError`, and process termination. The modeled impact is unauthenticated availability loss. It does not establish extraction, a filesystem write, confidentiality or integrity loss, sandbox escape, or code execution. Topology-identical four-file 7.5.20/7.5.21 fixtures retain request source `src/server.js:7`, list sink `src/storage.js:4`, and nine ordered propagators. Dependency-free witnesses isolate the vulnerable recursive walk in a child process and exercise the repaired 100-level bound over the same 12,000-segment shape. **Primary and comparative evidence.** Five reviewed 2026 advisories describe a sequence of distinct Link and SymbolicLink escape repairs in the npm `tar` package. GHSA-8qq5-rm4j-mr97 covers absolute hardlink targets and symlink poisoning through 7.5.2 ([first advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8qq5-rm4j-mr97)). GHSA-34x7-hfp2-rc4v shows that the 7.5.3 repair still validates parent segments relative to an entry directory while creating hardlinks relative to extraction `cwd`, and is affected below 7.5.7 ([parent-segment advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-34x7-hfp2-rc4v), [7.5.7 repair](https://github.com/isaacs/node-tar/commit/f4a7aa9)). GHSA-83g3-92jg-28cx uses two in-root symlinks to redirect a 7.5.7 hardlink target outside the root and is repaired in 7.5.8 ([symlink-chain advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-83g3-92jg-28cx)). GHSA-qffp-2rhf-9h96 demonstrates that `C:../target` passes the pre-strip check through 7.5.9 and becomes `../target` before hardlink creation ([drive-relative hardlink advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qffp-2rhf-9h96)). GHSA-9ppj-qmqm-q256 extends the same ordering defect to nested symlinks through 7.5.10; 7.5.11 strips the drive root before validating the rewritten target ([drive-relative symlink advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9ppj-qmqm-q256)). Authenticated code searches return zero `node-tar` and `tar.extract` hits in the current official CodeQL and Semgrep rule repositories. Existing generic archive-link guidance identifies risky extractor implementations but does not combine application source flow, the official API, installed package proof, and this complete patch sequence.

Version 7.5.10 creates `a/b/l -> ../../../secret.txt`; the write changes the external secret from `ORIGINAL` to `PWNED`. Version 7.5.11 creates no link and leaves the secret unchanged. Dependency-free witnesses separately show why resolving the drive-relative value before stripping appears contained, while resolving the rewritten value escapes. Require nearest exact production metadata or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 resolution. Remote request/upload data must reach the options `file`, a dynamic options object, or an HTTP request stream piped directly into extraction. Reject fixed local archives, create/list APIs, wrong packages, development-only metadata, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, binding reassignment, and wrapper shadowing. `preservePaths: false` cannot suppress an affected release because every reviewed bypass reaches the default supposedly secure path. An exact filter is strong counterevidence only if its callable logic rejects both `Link` and `SymbolicLink` before extraction; a single-type filter or merely inspecting path text remains candidate evidence.

Report only the concrete confidentiality or integrity boundary proved. Execution, persistence, or privilege escalation requires the corresponding writable executable, configuration, key, service, or startup target plus later consumption; do not infer it from a link primitive. Do not generalize the row to arbitrary member-name traversal, every tar parser, or npm package extraction, which separately filters links. ## 2026-08-23 — Model Fastify Static's router/normalizer guard bypass

**Primary and comparative evidence.** Reviewed GHSA-83w8-p2f5-377r / CVE-2026-15074 describes a high-severity disclosure when `@fastify/static` through 10.1.0 is used beside route-based middleware or guards ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-83w8-p2f5-377r)). Fastify's router does not collapse non-leading parent segments, so `/foo/../deep/secret.txt` and raw `%2e%2e` variants miss a guarded `/deep/*` route and match the static catch-all. The vulnerable plugin decodes the surviving path and delegates it to `@fastify/send`, whose normalization collapses the parent segment before its traversal guard. The 10.1.1 repair checks both the full decoded raw path and the post-prefix pathname, rejecting non-leading parent segments before either route-parameter consumption or downstream normalization can hide them ([upstream repair `db4276f`](https://github.com/fastify/fastify-static/commit/db4276f846ba56b21f93768cd6636ee5e2fc58b1)). Authenticated searches of the current official CodeQL and Semgrep rule repositories return no literal `@fastify/static` coverage. Generic source-to-filesystem queries are poorly positioned here because the application never passes request data to a visible filesystem API and the package's own final normalized path appears contained beneath its root.

**Executable boundary validation.** A safely removed isolated npm-alias matrix installs Fastify 5.12.1 with exact `@fastify/static` 10.1.0 and 10.1.1. Both applications register the upstream advisory's `app.all("/deep/*", ...401...)` guard over a static root containing `deep/secret.txt`. Direct access returns 401 on both releases. Version 10.1.0 returns the protected bytes with status 200 for raw `/foo/../deep/secret.txt`, lowercase `/%2e%2e/`, and uppercase `/%2E%2E/` requests. Version 10.1.1 rejects all three at 403. This demonstrates concrete confidentiality impact while also bounding the issue: normalization reaches another file inside the configured static root; the tested primitive does not escape that root or write a file.

**Model and precision decision.** Add a distinct `node-http-fastify-static-route-guard-bypass` identity with CWE-22. Require an official default, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS, or direct-require binding from exactly `@fastify/static`; an exact instance created by the official Fastify factory; registration with a root; nearest exact production or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 proof through 10.1.0; and a separate non-root wildcard route on the same non-reassigned instance whose handler or route options contain concrete authentication, authorization, permission, 401, or 403 behavior. Preserve exact and `lock-resolved-` sink provenance. Reject 10.1.1+, wrong modules or factory lookalikes, different guarded instances, public or unguarded static routes, handler-only file serving without a guard, missing roots/options, primitive options, development-only metadata, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, reassigned plugin or instance bindings, and wrapper shadowing. `serve: false` and `wildcard: false` prevent the affected catch-all and suppress the row. `allowedPath` remains a candidate control because only its actual runtime decision on the eventual protected normalized path can prove safety.

## 2026-08-23 — Detect vulnerable extract-zip applications without version-only overclaim

**Trigger and comparative evidence.** The reviewed high-severity GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv / CVE-2026-56876 establishes that `extract-zip` accepts archive symlink entries without validating their relative targets, allowing a contained member name to materialize a link outside the extraction directory. The advisory lists every published release through 2.0.1 as affected and no patched release ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv)). The official repository documents and exports one directly callable extraction function whose first argument is the archive path and whose options include the extraction directory plus an `onEntry` callback; its source deliberately creates Unix symlink entries ([official repository](https://github.com/max-mapper/extract-zip)). A current registry query confirms 2.0.1 is still the newest published artifact, despite an audit response describing a nonexistent 2.0.2 repair. Current public CodeQL and Semgrep rule-source searches return no literal `extract-zip` coverage. This makes a package-aware source-to-effect model useful beyond both generic Zip Slip member-name rules and version-only dependency alerts.

**Model decision and trust boundary.** Add a distinct `node-http-extract-zip-symlink-traversal` identity with CWE-22. Require the exact package and one of its official callable shapes: default ESM, TypeScript import-equals, CommonJS callable binding, or direct `require("extract-zip")(...)`. Resolve the nearest production declaration, accepting an exact published version through 2.0.1 or a fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock; preserve `lock-resolved-` sink provenance. The remote upload or request archive path must occupy argument zero, while argument one must exist and resolve to extraction options with a destination. Reject fixed archive paths, remote destination-only flow, missing options, wrong packages, development-only declarations, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent or v1 locks, stale metadata, binding reassignment, and wrapper shadowing. Keep a hypothetical 2.0.2 and later as future negative boundaries without representing 2.0.2 as currently installable.

**Mitigation and impact precision.** An `onEntry` callback is strong counterevidence only when its exact code derives the Unix type from `entry.externalFileAttributes` by shifting 16 bits, masks with `0o170000`/61440, compares with `0o120000`/40960, and throws on the symlink branch before extraction. Logging, returning a filename, post-extraction cleanup, and member-name containment do not constrain the link payload. Final review must establish the effective central-directory mode, decoded symlink target, extraction platform and privileges, final canonical link location, and a later application read or write through that link. Materializing an external link proves a directory-boundary violation but does not alone prove arbitrary-file read, overwrite, execution, persistence, or privilege escalation; those impacts require the corresponding later operation and accessible target.

**Benchmark and focused acceptance.** Add topology-identical four-file Express fixtures pinned to the same vulnerable 2.0.1 release. Both send `request.file.path` from `src/server.js:7` through three relative-import wrappers to `extract(path, options)` at `src/storage.js:4`, retain the same destination, callback shape, later configuration read, and nine ordered propagators. The vulnerable callback observes the symlink and returns its name; the control throws before extraction, so only the positive emits the framework row. Dependency-free witnesses prove that a contained member name can resolve its symlink payload to protected configuration outside the root and that the exact mode guard fails closed on the same entry. Six regression groups cover all official bindings, the complete published vulnerable boundary, the future repair boundary, argument roles, options, reassignment, shadowing, exact mitigation, observe-only callbacks, exact and lock proof, cross-file flow, reviewer language, and strict pair integrity. The perfect-gate specialized pair and three-run canonical integration advance the corpus to 74 exploit/control pairs and 444 scans. Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript, witnesses, PostCSS and `tmp` sibling models, scanner-owned ZIP extraction, archive link-pivot logic, and residual inventory pass on Windows with 90 tests, 1,137 assertions, one intentional platform skip, and no failures; native Ubuntu/WSL passes all 91 tests and 1,138 assertions. Full scanner, compiled self-review, package, desktop, Linux GUI, and hosted exact-head evidence will be appended after the pushed implementation checkpoint completes those gates.

**Final acceptance evidence.** Exact implementation checkpoint `f83fed64cd99e699b7314621ce61396251215c1d` passes the authoritative Bun 1.3.14 suite with 1,280 tests, 9,666 assertions, 20 intentional environment/platform skips, and zero failures across 140 files in 319.95 seconds. Formatting, generated output, TypeScript, the clean production build, both host-focused lanes, and `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` are green with no known vulnerabilities. ## 2026-08-23 — Own the plugin ZIP policy instead of trusting a symlink-capable wrapper

**Trigger and evidence.** The fail-closed production audit began reporting high-severity GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv / CVE-2026-56876 against the scanner's direct `extract-zip` 2.0.1 dependency. The reviewed advisory describes unvalidated relative symlink targets escaping the extraction directory and lists every published release through 2.0.1 as affected with no patched version ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv)). The npm audit response claimed a hypothetical `>=2.0.2` repair, but a direct registry query on 2026-08-23 returned no such version; the published sequence still ends at 2.0.1 ([authoritative registry document](https://registry.npmjs.org/extract-zip)). Suppressing the advisory would make packaging green without changing the dependency graph. Retaining the wrapper merely because the existing `onEntry` callback rejected Unix symlink mode before that wrapper's symlink branch would also leave policy correctness coupled to undocumented callback ordering and an audited component that intentionally supports symlink creation.

**Decision.** Remove `extract-zip` and its twelve-package subtree. Use current `yauzl` 3.4.0 as the narrow ZIP parser/decompressor and keep all extraction policy in scanner-owned code. Yauzl's documented design reads the central directory, supports lazy bounded entry processing, validates effective filenames, and enforces declared decoded sizes, while deliberately leaving extraction policy to its caller ([official yauzl design and API](https://github.com/thejoshwolfe/yauzl#readme)). The scanner first opens a non-symlink regular archive with no-follow semantics where available, caps the compressed snapshot at 256 MiB, verifies file identity before and after the read, and uses that single immutable buffer for both complete preflight and extraction. This removes the validate/reopen race and ensures no regular member is written before a later malicious entry has been seen.

**Fail-closed archive contract.** Raw central-directory validation rejects ZIP64, more than 4,096 entries, central directories over 16 MiB, invalid bounds or records, and backslash-qualified raw names before the library can normalize them. Decoded validation independently applies scanner path rules; lowercases collision keys for Windows-portable duplicate detection; rejects a file that is an explicit ancestor of another entry; rejects symlinks and every non-regular/non-directory Unix type; rejects encryption, unsupported decoding, nonempty directory records, entries over 128 MiB, and aggregate expansion over 512 MiB. Extraction ignores `__MACOSX` metadata, creates only mode-0700 directories and mode-0600 regular files under a scanner-created staging root, uses exclusive creation, streams one entry at a time, propagates cancellation, relies on yauzl's decoded-size enforcement, and then rereads every file to compare CRC-32. Any error removes staging before the destination rename. The destination remains atomic at the directory level.

**Regression boundary.** A valid two-file plugin proves the normal root and nested-file path. A crafted central-directory entry with Unix symlink mode and a `../../outside.txt` payload reproduces the advisory's dangerous shape; the regression proves rejection occurs before `plugin.json` is extracted, the external sentinel remains unchanged, and the destination never appears. Separate cases cover decoded parent traversal, raw backslash traversal, and a regular-file/child topology conflict. The focused suite passes 16 tests and 78 assertions on Windows Bun 1.3.14 and native Ubuntu/WSL Bun 1.3.14. Generated-model drift, TypeScript, a clean production build, and `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level high` are green with no known vulnerabilities. Full scanner, package, desktop, Linux GUI, and hosted exact-head evidence will be appended after the pushed repair checkpoint completes those gates.

**Final acceptance evidence.** Exact repair checkpoint `f0dd3f248f923e86fc915e54a44793e1b95abc79` passes the complete Bun 1.3.14 suite with 1,274 tests, 9,633 assertions, 20 intentional environment/platform skips, and zero failures across 139 files in 311.37 seconds. Formatting, generated output, TypeScript, clean production build, both host-focused archive lanes, and the fail-closed production advisory audit are green. Strict inspection validates a 251-entry, 1,629,795-byte archive with SHA-1 `1fd4819d0b6aeeed50b04a943fb044a54445d56b` and SHA-256 `1bf815aa3f629f8046d2b2db7bd9e02832017c29af11380175142f921deeb2af`. Three isolated Windows installs add 67 packages each and two Ubuntu Node 22.23.1 installs add 75 each; every install validates public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled plugin files. The smaller installed graphs reflect removal of the vulnerable wrapper's twelve-package subtree. The archive is safely removed after validation.

Windows builds without warnings or errors, passes 7/7 scanner-core plus 3/3 shared-desktop tests, and publishes a 346,796-byte executable with SHA-256 `3dd8e5dd2dd728ba9ee00939099bfb949acd2d3ab2c1108ae433735d6195b2e5`. The new ambient .NET 10 SDK initially found no selected NuGet source for the .NET 8 runtime and ILLink packs during publication; an explicit restore from the repository-pinned NuGet.org source retained vulnerability auditing and allowed a no-restore publication, without suppressing `NU1900`. WSL performs locked restores and a warning-free build, passes 7/7 core, 3/3 shared, and 2/2 Linux GUI tests, then passes non-graphical and real X11/Xvfb startup. Its 72,568-byte executable has SHA-256 `53c4e49e6f0aecdafec913a4d5b2423d70503f35db12c5228c0e25768fc6421d`. All exact-head workflows pass without retry: [Node `32674631773`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631773), [Windows GUI `32674631925`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631925), [Linux GUI `32674631841`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631841), [container `32674631894`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631894), [.NET `32674631827`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631827), [Go `32674631800`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631800), and [Java `32674631799`](https://github.com/secwest/copilot-security/actions/runs/32674631799).

## 2026-08-07 — Bind PostCSS previous-map disclosure to implicit loading and output exposure

**Evidence and scanner comparison.** GitHub's reviewed GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 identifies PostCSS through 8.5.17 as vulnerable when attacker-controlled CSS supplies a final external `sourceMappingURL`: default parsing and processing load that previous `.map` relative to `opts.from`, or accept an absolute annotation when `from` is absent. The 8.5.18 repair uses `path.relative`, separator-aware `..` rejection, and an absolute-path check to keep default loading in the CSS file's directory; `unsafeMap: true` is the documented opt-out. Authenticated current-source searches find zero `postcss` hits in CodeQL and public Semgrep rules. CodeQL's two `sourceMappingURL` hits are a source-map comment library and its library test, not a security query. A safely removed real npm-alias matrix confirms protected `sourcesContent` disclosure under 8.5.17, rejection under 8.5.18, exact protection from `map: false`, and intentional re-enablement by `unsafeMap: true` on the repaired release.

**Model and impact boundary.** Add `node-http-postcss-source-map-traversal` with CWE-22. Bind official root, named parse, processor, ESM, TypeScript import-equals, and CommonJS forms to exactly `postcss`; require nearest exact runtime or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 proof through 8.5.17. Retain only remote CSS at argument zero of `parse` or `process`; exact `map: false` and `map: { prev: false }` prevent annotation loading. Patched/development-only dependencies, fixed CSS, wrong packages, reassigned members or receivers, wrapper shadows, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, and stale metadata fail closed. Review must prove a final non-inline annotation ending in `.map`, traversal or absolute resolution outside the intended directory, a valid source map, and an exposed `result.map`, input map, emitted artifact, API response, or `sourcesContent` channel. A file read alone does not prove disclosure; versions 8.5.12 through 8.5.17 do not justify arbitrary non-`.map` read or code-execution claims.

**Benchmark.** A topology-identical four-file Express pair sends a CSS body from `src/server.js:8` through three relative-import wrappers to `postcss([]).process` at `src/storage.js:5`, then returns the generated map. The 8.5.17 positive retains nine ordered propagators and CWE-22; the 8.5.18 control emits no row. Dependency-free witnesses reproduce external protected-map loading and the repaired relative-path rejection. Five regression groups cover binding and operation forms, exact map disablement, negative identity/version/source cases, lock proof, typed cross-file flow, and reviewer bounds. The strict pair advances the canonical corpus to 73 exploit/control pairs and 438 repeated scans.

**Final acceptance evidence.** The exact-head acceptance above also closes the PostCSS increment. Two full-repository compiled reviews of a private tracked-head archive take 20,516 and 10,315 ms and produce 96 byte-identical rows, 212,721 bytes, and SHA-256 `7aee83dfb79bf8a8bdcb2f9df339037e862865e3f23916914af0d98c7d255a8b`; 92 rows are rooted in benchmark fixtures. The PostCSS positive retains its exact source line 8, sink line 5, `vulnerable-postcss-process-source-map-traversal` provenance, CWE-22, and nine propagators, while the 8.5.18 twin is absent. The preceding `tmp` row retains the same exact topology and its repaired twin remains absent. The first attempted acceptance harness invoked `git archive` from `sdk/typescript`, which Git correctly scoped to that subdirectory; those measurements were discarded before documentation. The corrected harness invokes archive construction from the repository root and asserts benchmark-fixture presence plus both package model identities before recording evidence.

## 2026-08-07 — Bind tmp path traversal to creator, option, version, and containment semantics

**Scanner comparison and primary evidence.** GitHub's reviewed GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65 / CVE-2026-44705 identifies path traversal when untrusted `prefix`, `postfix`, or `dir` reaches `tmp` below 0.2.6 and names 0.2.6 as the repair ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-ph9p-34f9-6g65)). The upstream patch also validates `template`, rejects relative filename components, and replaces `resolvedPath.startsWith(tmpDir)` with a `path.relative` plus absolute-path boundary, closing the sibling-name confusion where `base-escape` shares the textual prefix `base` ([upstream repair `efa4a06`](https://github.com/raszi/node-tmp/commit/efa4a06)). The official API distinguishes creators `file`/`fileSync`/`dir`/`dirSync` from `tmpName`/`tmpNameSync`, which return names without creating filesystem objects, and documents all four path-shaping options ([official 0.2.6 API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raszi/node-tmp/v0.2.6/README.md)). Authenticated current-source searches return zero `node-tmp` hits in CodeQL and public Semgrep. CodeQL's only `tmp.fileSync` occurrence is a secure-temporary-file CWE-377 example, not a package/version/options model; its high-precision Zip Slip query follows attacker-controlled archive entry paths into filesystem writes, a different source and construction boundary ([CodeQL example](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/main/javascript/ql/src/Security/CWE-377/examples/secure-temporary-file.js), [CodeQL Zip Slip query](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/javascript/js-zipslip/), [Semgrep public rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules)).

**Executable boundary validation.** A safely removed isolated npm-alias matrix runs real 0.2.5 and 0.2.6 packages with separate controlled roots. Under 0.2.5, `fileSync({tmpdir: base, prefix: "../escaped"})` creates a path whose relative form begins outside `base`. Its earlier directory guard is independently bypassed with `dir: "../base-escape"`: the resolved sibling path begins with the base string but is outside the base directory. Version 0.2.6 rejects the first with `Relative value not allowed` and the second because the computed relative directory begins `..`. Published npm metadata confirms the exact 0.2.5 and 0.2.6 artifacts and the complete 0.x release sequence through current 0.2.7.

**Model decision and precision boundary.** Add `node-http-tmp-path-traversal` with CWE-22. Accept official default, namespace, TypeScript import-equals, named or aliased ESM, destructured CommonJS, direct CommonJS member, and CommonJS receiver bindings to exactly `tmp`. Require the nearest exact runtime declaration or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock below 0.2.6. Only `file`, `fileSync`, `dir`, and `dirSync` establish the modeled creation effect; name generation alone requires a separately proven later filesystem effect and is deliberately excluded. Parse only `prefix`, `postfix`, `template`, and `dir` from literal options. A dynamic options object or spread is retained only while it can still supply at least one path-shaping field; an object spread followed by fixed definitions of all four is negative. Request data used only for `keep`, `mode`, `tries`, cleanup, or descriptor policy is irrelevant. Patched versions, fixed options, wrong packages/methods, development-only declarations, receiver or member reassignment, wrapper shadowing, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, stale metadata, and primitive callback-shaped first arguments fail closed. `path.basename` and strict filename-component allowlists remain candidate controls for review, never automatic safety claims.

**Impact boundary.** The package uses exclusive creation and includes process/random material in generated names. A report must prove a platform-relevant separator, traversal component, absolute/sibling containment bypass, or equivalent runtime value; the exact configured `tmpdir`; the resulting canonical path outside that boundary; and a concrete confidentiality, integrity, isolation, or availability effect. Directory escape and attacker-influenced placement do not by themselves prove overwrite of a chosen existing file, execution, persistence, or container escape. Cleanup after creation does not prevent the boundary violation, while an exact pre-creation rejection or canonical relative containment check is strong counterevidence.

**Benchmark and focused acceptance.** A topology-identical four-file Express pair sends a query prefix through three relative-import wrappers into `tmp.fileSync`; the 0.2.5 positive writes protected export contents through the returned descriptor, while the 0.2.6 control retains every source, wrapper, creator, option, and write line. The positive emits source `src/server.js:8`, sink `src/storage.js:5`, CWE-22, and nine ordered propagators; the control emits no row. Dependency-free witnesses create and read the escaped content under a private temporary root, clean it safely, and prove repaired rejection without installing a vulnerable package. Eight direct regressions cover all supported bindings and creator forms, every path-shaping option, dynamic/spread options and complete overwrite, exact and lock proof, repaired/development/wrong/fixed/reassigned/shadowed cases, basename control retention, dense candidates, prompt guidance, pair integrity, and cross-file topology. ## 2026-08-07 — Synthesize global prototype writes with Axios read-side gadgets

**Scanner comparison and primary evidence.** Authenticated current-source searches of the public CodeQL and Semgrep rule repositories returned zero matches for either `axios` plus prototype pollution or `axios` plus `config.proxy`; CodeQL's public JavaScript coverage remains generic prototype-polluting assignment/function/merge analysis, and Semgrep's public community source has no Axios gadget rule ([CodeQL prototype-pollution customization](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/codeql-cli/latest/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/security/dataflow/PrototypePollutionCustomizations.qll), [Semgrep JavaScript rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules/tree/develop/javascript)). Axios's reviewed 2026 advisories describe a materially different read-side problem: a separate same-process prototype primitive can supply inherited request configuration. The original direct path reads inherited `proxy`, `auth`, `baseURL`, `socketPath`, `beforeRedirect`, or `insecureHTTPParser`; later null-prototype configuration hardening closes that path, but ordinary request interceptors that return `{...config}` or `Object.assign({}, config)` can rematerialize a normal object before dispatch ([direct configuration/transform advisory GHSA-3g43-6gmg-66jw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3g43-6gmg-66jw), [HTTP adapter gadget advisory GHSA-q8qp-cvcw-x6jj](https://github.com/axios/axios/security/advisories/GHSA-q8qp-cvcw-x6jj), [interceptor bypass GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9)). This is precisely where an attack-path scanner can improve on isolated source-to-sink rules: the Axios call is harmless without the earlier state write, and the state write's impact is materially sharper when the later request carries authorization or body data.

**Executable boundary validation.** Two temporary, safely removed npm-alias matrices exercised real Lodash and Axios distributions over loopback HTTP with every ambient proxy variable cleared. The first attempt deliberately failed to pollute with a simple `__proto__` object and corrected the witness to Lodash 4.17.10's historically accurate `constructor.prototype` traversal. With that payload, Axios 1.15.1 sent the absolute target URL, `Bearer header-secret`, and request body to the attacker proxy without an interceptor. Axios 1.15.2, 1.16.0, and 1.17.0 stayed on the intended target until a same-instance spread interceptor was installed; Axios 1.17.0 then routed through the attacker proxy, while 1.18.0 and current 1.19.0 did not. Lodash 4.17.11 never installed `Object.prototype.proxy`. A second matrix confirmed that an identity interceptor remains null-prototype-safe, top-level spread and `Object.assign({}, config)` copies are both vulnerable on 1.17.0, and an own `proxy:false` in the returned copy, instance configuration, or request configuration closes that post-hardening proxy route. On 1.15.1, however, both call-level and instance-level `proxy:false` stopped routing but failed in inherited option validation with `TypeError: validator is not a function`; the control reduces confidentiality/integrity impact but does not establish availability safety.

**Model decision.** `node-http-axios-prototype-gadget-chain` is generated only from an already proven object-valued global write: version-aware recursive merge, `js-toml.load`, `flat.unflatten`, or the value position of vulnerable `dset/merge`. Deletion primitives, Immutable.js's returned-object-only replacement, `Object.assign` target prototype replacement, generic path writes whose value class is unknown, test/example code, different nearest manifests, development-only Axios declarations, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent or v1 locks, wrong packages, and reassigned or shadowed receivers fail closed. Axios has two exact stages: 0.19.0–0.31.0 and 1.0.0–1.15.1 produce a direct gadget row; 0.31.1–0.32.x and 1.15.2–1.17.x require an earlier top-level plain-object-copy request interceptor on the same official receiver. Version 0.33.0 and 1.18.0 are repaired. For the second stage, any preserved own `proxy:false` suppresses the row; for the first, it is retained as a candidate control because the live validator failure remains. The synthesized schema-1.2 path preserves the original remote source and up to nine wrapper propagators, names the exact prototype state-write sink, records Axios manifest/lock proof, the interceptor-copy line, shared `Object.prototype.proxy` state, and the final outbound call with CWE-1321 and CWE-441. When that chain exists, only the exact lower-level primitive record with the same source, state-write path, line, and sink kind is removed. This consolidation prevented a duplicate new Lodash row from displacing the older exact Lodash benchmark at the fixed 96-row repository cap and gives the reviewer one complete reportable path instead of two fragments.

**Benchmark design.** The positive fixture sends `request.body` through three relative imports to exact Lodash 4.17.10 merge, then executes an Axios 1.17.0 instance request after a spread interceptor. Its control preserves every source, wrapper, merge, interceptor, and request line while pinning Lodash 4.17.11 and Axios 1.18.0. Dependency-free witnesses prove the global object-valued write, loss and restoration of the null-prototype boundary, absence of an own proxy property, inherited proxy selection, protected request material, both repairs, and cleanup without installing a vulnerable dependency. The strict manifest requires both CWEs, high/critical severity, validation, attack-path analysis, code evidence, perfect precision/recall/stability/evidence gates, and zero false positives. Seven direct tests cover both 0.x/1.x release stages; ESM, namespace, and CommonJS roots or instances; spread and `Object.assign` copies; identity and own-proxy controls; exact and fresh consistent npm v2/v3 proof; wrong, repaired, development-only, reassigned, shadowed, local-only, cross-boundary, and dense candidates; exact state/dependency/interceptor propagators; benchmark topology; and the consolidation invariant. The canonical corpus is now 71 exploit/control pairs and 426 repeated scans.

**Focused acceptance.** The new chain, prior Axios SSRF, full package-aware merge family, and canonical corpus tests initially exposed and then verified the consolidation correction. The final widened set also includes Lodash deletion, Immutable.js replacement, `object-path`, `dset`, `flat`, `jsonpath-plus`, and `js-toml`. Native Ubuntu WSL Bun 1.3.14 passes all 96 tests and 1,757 assertions with no skips or failures across the same 11 files in 437.41 seconds. ## 2026-08-07 — Model Immutable.js object-local prototype replacement

**Scanner comparison and primary evidence.** Reviewed GHSA-wf6x-7x77-mvgw / CVE-2026-29063 describes a high-severity Immutable.js family in which plain-object merge and conversion paths accept an own `__proto__` key and produce an object with attacker-controlled inherited fields. Current CodeQL has an official Immutable framework model, but it supplies only generic collection construction, storage, load, conversion, and merge flow; its generic extend catalog does not include Immutable, and current public Semgrep source searches contain neither an Immutable rule nor `mergeDeep` ([reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-wf6x-7x77-mvgw), [CodeQL Immutable framework](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/main/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/frameworks/Immutable.qll), [CodeQL extend framework](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/main/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/Extend.qll), [Semgrep community JavaScript rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules/tree/develop/javascript)). The upstream repair adds a shared magic-key predicate to plain-object merge, set, shallow-copy, `toObject`, and `toJS` paths; its tests expressly distinguish returned-object inheritance from global pollution ([main repair `16b3313`](https://github.com/immutable-js/immutable-js/commit/16b3313), [4.x port `6ed4eb6`](https://github.com/immutable-js/immutable-js/commit/6ed4eb6), [3.x port `6e2cf1c`](https://github.com/immutable-js/immutable-js/commit/6e2cf1c)).

**Executable release and API matrix.** Six isolated npm aliases establish the real stable boundaries. Version 3.8.2 replaces the output prototype through `Map(payload).toObject()`, `Map(payload).toJS()`, and `fromJS(payload).toJS()`; its functional plain-object merge/set/update shape is unavailable. Version 3.8.3 blocks all three conversions. Versions 4.3.7 and 5.1.4 replace returned or nested object prototypes through `merge`, `mergeWith`, `mergeDeep`, `mergeDeepWith`, `set`, `setIn`, `update`, `updateIn`, and the three conversion forms. Versions 4.3.8 and 5.1.5 block every tested path, resolving the advisory prose/table ambiguity in favor of the published 4.3.8 security release ([v4.3.8 release](https://github.com/immutable-js/immutable-js/releases/tag/v4.3.8), [v5.1.5 release](https://github.com/immutable-js/immutable-js/releases/tag/v5.1.5)). Target-only `merge(payload, fixed)` is vulnerable because the API copies argument zero; `mergeWith` is affected through the same internal merge path. By contrast, `remove`/`removeIn` do not reproduce the effect, and a remote value passed under a fixed safe `set` key remains ordinary nested data. Every vulnerable result has inherited `admin`, no own `admin`, and an attacker-controlled immediate prototype while `({}).admin` remains undefined.

**Decision and precision contract.** Add `node-http-immutable-prototype-replacement` with CWE-1321. Accept official named/aliased/destructured functions, namespace or interoperable default receivers, CommonJS receivers and direct members, direct constructor/conversion chains, and one locally retained `Map`/`fromJS` collection. Require nearest exact runtime or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock evidence. Conversion surfaces are eligible below 3.8.3, on 4.x below 4.3.8, and on 5.x below 5.1.5; functional surfaces are eligible only on modeled vulnerable 4.x/5.x releases. For `merge`/`mergeDeep`, every argument is relevant. For `mergeWith`/`mergeDeepWith`, every operand after the merger callback is relevant. For `set`, `setIn`, `update`, and `updateIn`, argument zero and key/path argument one are relevant; a remote argument two is relevant only beneath a statically magic path. Fresh lock proof prepends `lock-resolved-`. Reject repaired branches, 3.x functional guesses, safe-key value-only flow, wrong/read-only APIs or packages, unconnected same-line source/conversion expressions, absent sources, receiver/member/value reassignment, wrapper shadowing, development-only declarations, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, and stale metadata. A 64-candidate package-local bound retains the valid row after forty unrelated calls.

**Impact and benchmark boundary.** This primitive generally replaces only the returned or nested application's plain-object prototype. It does not establish global `Object.prototype` mutation, cross-object influence, or code execution. Final review must prove that the deployed parser preserves an own `__proto__` key, identify the exact output object whose prototype changes, distinguish inherited from own security fields, and trace a later authorization, integrity, disclosure, availability, or other security decision that consumes the inherited value. A topology-identical four-file Express 5.1.4/5.1.5 pair retains source `src/server.js:8`, sink `src/storage.js:4`, and nine ordered propagators; only 5.1.4 emits `vulnerable-immutable-merge-deep-prototype-replacement`. Dependency-free witnesses reproduce inherited `admin` authorization and repaired rejection without changing the global prototype. A strict specialized pair and three canonical runs advance the corpus to 70 exploit/control pairs and 420 scans.

**Focused acceptance.** Seven direct regressions cover supported bindings, functional and conversion APIs, all three repair branches, exact and lock proof, every relevant operand class, safe fixed-key values, merger-only flow, wrong package/API, absent or unrelated same-line sources, unconnected conversions, reassignment, development metadata, candidate density, prompt guidance, pair integrity, and repository-cap retention. Formatting, generated output, TypeScript, both witnesses, the prior Lodash deletion, `object-path`, `dset`, `flat`, `jsonpath-plus`, and `js-toml` suites, and the canonical pair gate pass on Windows in 92.14 seconds and native Ubuntu WSL Bun 1.3.14 in 371.78 seconds with 66 tests, 1,518 assertions, and no failures on each platform. Full scanner, compiled self-review, package, desktop, WSL GUI, and hosted exact-head evidence will be appended only after the pushed implementation checkpoint completes those gates.

## 2026-08-07 — Model Lodash's two-stage unset/omit prototype deletion

**Scanner comparison and primary evidence.** Current CodeQL recognizes `unset` and `omit` as generic Lodash API members, but its public prototype-pollution customization exposes only tainted recursive-extension sinks; current public Semgrep rule-source searches return no Lodash `unset` or `omit` rule ([CodeQL Lodash framework model](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/codeql-cli/latest/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/frameworks/LodashUnderscore.qll), [CodeQL prototype-pollution customization](https://github.com/github/codeql/blob/codeql-cli/latest/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/security/dataflow/PrototypePollutionCustomizations.qll), [Semgrep community JavaScript rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules/tree/develop/javascript)). Two reviewed Lodash advisories establish a distinct deletion primitive. The original repair covers 4.0.0 through 4.17.22 and attempts to block `__proto__` plus `constructor.prototype`; the follow-up proves that 4.17.23 still accepts array-wrapped segments and primitive roots, permitting deletion from built-in prototypes through `unset` and core `omit` ([original advisory GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg), [array-bypass advisory GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh), [completed repair `fe8d32e`](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/commit/fe8d32e)). This is not a recursive merge or value-injection sink: it removes an existing shared property and cannot replace its behavior.

**Executable package and call matrix.** Isolated npm installs exercise core Lodash 4.17.21, 4.17.23, and 4.18.0; `lodash-es` 4.17.23/4.18.0; `lodash-amd` 4.17.23/4.18.0; `lodash.unset` 4.5.2/4.18.0; and `lodash.omit` 4.5.0/4.18.0. Core 4.17.21 deletes `Object.prototype.toString` through ordinary and nested-array `__proto__` paths and deletes `Number.prototype.toFixed` through primitive-root `constructor.prototype`. Version 4.17.23 rejects the ordinary `__proto__` string but still deletes through `[["__proto__"], "toString"]`, array-wrapped constructor/prototype segments, and primitive roots. Version 4.18.0 rejects all tested forms. The ES build matches core behavior. The AMD package is an actual AMD distribution rather than a CommonJS receiver, so the supported source form binds the configured `lodash` module through `define`/`require`. The standalone `lodash.unset` 4.5.2 is vulnerable and 4.18.0 repaired. Core `omit` requires the attacker path at its path-list nesting depth; a superficially similar flat array is inert. Separately published `lodash.omit` 4.5.0 does not delete the tested shared members and the reviewed affected-package list omits it, so dependency-name similarity cannot authorize a finding. npm deprecates the 4.18.0 core/ES/AMD distributions as bad releases; the benchmark therefore pins current 4.18.1 as its deployable control while preserving 4.18.0 as the semantic security boundary ([Lodash 4.18 release notes](https://github.com/lodash/lodash/releases/tag/4.18.0), [core npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash), [`lodash.unset` npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lodash.unset)).

**Decision and precision contract.** Add `node-http-lodash-prototype-deletion` with CWE-1321. Accept official core default/namespace/CommonJS receivers, named or destructured methods, direct require members, and `lodash/unset` or `lodash/omit` subpaths; equivalent ESM forms for `lodash-es`; an AMD callback receiver only when the nearest runtime declaration is `lodash-amd`; and direct default/CommonJS `lodash.unset`. Require 4.x below 4.18.0. Preserve `unset` path argument one and every `omit` path operand after target argument zero. Releases through 4.17.22 emit ordinary method/package sink kinds; exactly 4.17.23 emits `array-path` provenance so final review must prove nested-array or primitive-root shape. Fresh npm v2/v3 resolution prepends `lock-resolved-`. Reject pre-4 and 4.18+ releases, target-only flow, read-only APIs, wrong packages or methods, `lodash.omit`, unsupported namespace guesses, API/member reassignment, wrapper shadowing, missing sources, development-only declarations, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, and stale metadata. A 64-candidate package-local bound retains a valid sink after forty unrelated calls.

**Impact and benchmark boundary.** Deletion is security-relevant only if the runtime target/path reaches a built-in or other shared prototype, the named property exists and is configurable, the deletion occurs before a security-sensitive later operation, and application error handling permits the effect to survive long enough to matter. Final review must prove parser preservation of every path segment and nesting level, distinguish core `omit`'s list-of-paths shape from a single path, name the deleted member, trace every dependent authorization, integrity, or availability operation, and account for cleanup plus process lifetime. Code execution or property injection requires an independent primitive or gadget and cannot be inferred from this row.

Seven direct regressions cover all supported package and binding identities, both methods and repair stages, exact and lock proof, target/method/package confusion, no source, reassignment, shadowing, candidate density, prompt guidance, pair integrity, and repository-cap retention. ## 2026-08-07 — Model object-path's mode-sensitive three-stage repair history

**Scanner comparison and primary evidence.** Current public CodeQL and Semgrep rule-source searches contain no literal `object-path`, `set-value`, or `dot-prop` package model ([CodeQL JavaScript security libraries](https://github.com/github/codeql/tree/main/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/security), [Semgrep community JavaScript rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules/tree/develop/javascript)). `object-path` provides the broadest distinct improvement because three reviewed advisories cover separate behaviors: inherited-mode `set` prototype pollution before 0.11.5, a nested-array type-confusion bypass before 0.11.6, and inherited-mode `del` pollution before 0.11.8 ([original `set` advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cwx2-736x-mf6w), [array bypass advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v39p-96qg-c8rf), [later `del` advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8v63-cqqc-6r2c)). The official 0.11.8 changelog expands the last repair to `del`, `empty`, `push`, and `insert`, explicitly states that the 0.11.0+ default instance is unaffected, and documents both `withInheritedProps` and `create({includeInheritedProps:true})` ([official v0.11.8 API and changelog](https://github.com/mariocasciaro/object-path/tree/v0.11.8), [final repair `4f0903f`](https://github.com/mariocasciaro/object-path/commit/4f0903fd7c832d12ccbe0d9c3d7e25d985e9e884)).

**Executable seven-release matrix.** Isolated installs of 0.10.0, 0.11.0, 0.11.4, 0.11.5, 0.11.6, 0.11.7, and 0.11.8 execute ordinary-string and nested-array paths across base and inherited receivers. Version 0.10.0's base `set`, `ensureExists`, `push`, and `insert` traverse `Object.prototype`; its `del` and `empty` do not, matching the 0.10.0 breaking change that made those operations ignore non-own properties. From 0.11.0, the base instance is own-property-only and every tested primitive is negative. In inherited mode, all six mutating methods are vulnerable through 0.11.4. Version 0.11.5 makes ordinary-string `set` and `ensureExists` throw but still accepts `[["__proto__"], "polluted"]`; 0.11.6 closes that bypass. Inherited `del`, `empty`, `push`, and `insert` remain executable through 0.11.7 and all throw before prototype access in 0.11.8. A separate 0.9.3 direct `set` regression retains the original advisory's earlier-0.x surface without pretending later methods existed on every historical line.

**Decision and precision contract.** Add `node-http-object-path-prototype-pollution` with CWE-1321. Require nearest exact runtime or fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock evidence. Track the package's official CommonJS receiver and interoperable default import, direct or destructured method bindings, `withInheritedProps`, literal `create({includeInheritedProps:true})`, aliases, method aliases, and callable object-bound instances. Preserve the receiver shape because unbound methods take the path at argument one, while `objectPath(target)`, an inherited receiver called with a target, or a configured receiver called with a target produces bound methods whose path is argument zero. Before 0.11.0, emit method-specific `vulnerable-object-path-legacy-*` only for `set` on earlier 0.x releases and for `set`, `ensureExists`, `push`, or `insert` from 0.10.0. For 0.11.x inherited mode, emit `vulnerable-object-path-inherited-set` or `-ensure-exists` below 0.11.6 and `-del`, `-empty`, `-push`, or `-insert` below 0.11.8. Fresh lock proof prepends `lock-resolved-`. Reject the 0.11.0+ default instance, pre-inherited `del`/`empty`, false, absent, or dynamic inherited configuration, repaired method/version combinations, target-only or value-only request flow, read-only methods, namespace guesses, wrong packages or members, API/method reassignment, wrapper shadowing, missing sources, development-only declarations, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, and unsafe metadata. A 64-candidate package-local bound retains a sink after forty unrelated calls without activating unrelated files.

**Impact and deletion semantics.** Deterministic inventory establishes an API/mode/version/position-correct primitive; final reporting still requires the runtime path representation, parser preservation of string or nested-array segments, the exact built-in or application prototype reached, and concrete downstream use. Mutation and deletion are distinct. Deleting `Object.prototype.toString` under 0.11.7 causes later `String({})` coercion to throw because no primitive conversion remains, but cleanup restores the method; an application finding must prove the process lifetime, error boundary, cross-request reachability, and availability or other impact. Version 0.11.5's ordinary-string exception is not a control for attacker-controlled arrays, while the 0.11.6 type normalization and 0.11.8 pre-access magic-property rejection are strong counterevidence for their exact repaired surfaces.

**Executable benchmark and focused acceptance.** Add topology-identical four-file Express fixtures at vulnerable 0.11.7 and repaired 0.11.8. Both retain source `src/server.js:8`, sink `src/storage.js:4`, and nine ordered relative-import/call/parameter propagators; only 0.11.7 emits `vulnerable-object-path-inherited-del` with CWE-1321. Dependency-free witnesses reproduce deletion, the concrete coercion failure, cleanup, and the repaired guard. A strict specialized pair and three-run canonical cases advance the corpus to 68 exploit/control pairs and 408 scans. Eight direct regressions cover the seven-release matrix plus 0.9.3, every mutating method, three receiver modes, literal configuration, bound/unbound argument positions, all supported binding forms, exact/optional/lock proof, API/package/argument confusion, no source, reassignment, shadowing, candidate density, prompt guidance, pair integrity, and repository-cap retention. ## 2026-08-07 — Model dset's nested-path and merge-value prototype pollution

**Scanner comparison and primary evidence.** Current public CodeQL and Semgrep JavaScript rule-source searches contain no literal `dset` package model ([CodeQL JavaScript security libraries](https://github.com/github/codeql/tree/main/javascript/ql/lib/semmle/javascript/security), [Semgrep community JavaScript rules](https://github.com/semgrep/semgrep-rules/tree/develop/javascript)). Three reviewed advisories describe successive incomplete repairs: GHSA-q4xc-7cw8-cgfj / CVE-2020-28277 covers the original path primitive, GHSA-23wx-cgxq-vpwx / CVE-2022-25645 covers recursive pollution from the `dset/merge` value, and GHSA-f6v4-cf5j-vf3w / CVE-2024-21529 covers the later path-type bypass ([original path advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q4xc-7cw8-cgfj), [merge-value advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-23wx-cgxq-vpwx), [nested-path advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f6v4-cf5j-vf3w)). The final upstream repair converts each path element to a string before comparing it with `__proto__`, `constructor`, and `prototype`, closing an implicit-coercion gap left by the earlier comparison ([upstream repair `16d6154`](https://github.com/lukeed/dset/commit/16d6154e085bef01e99f01330e5a421a7f098afa)). This package primitive is not equivalent to the scanner's generic application property-write model because exploitability depends on published entry point, export shape, release, argument position, and runtime path type.

**Live release and API matrix.** Isolated npm installs establish the boundary instead of copying inconsistent advisory metadata. Versions 1.0.1, 2.0.0, and 2.0.1 expose a directly callable CommonJS/default function and accept ordinary dangerous strings, arrays, and nested arrays. Version 2.1.0 blocks ordinary strings and flat arrays but still accepts `[["__proto__"], "polluted"]`, because the array object fails strict string comparison and is coerced only during property access. Versions 3.0.0 through 3.1.3 expose the named `dset` function and preserve that nested-array bypass; 3.1.4 blocks it. This proves live-vulnerable 2.0.1 despite the oldest advisory's stale machine-readable `<2.0.1` cutoff. The `dset/merge` entry point begins at 3.1.0: remote values recursively merge into an existing destination and pollute under 3.1.0/3.1.1, while 3.1.2/3.1.3 reject dangerous recursive keys; its path argument retains the separate nested-array bypass until 3.1.4.

**Decision and precision contract.** Add a distinct `node-http-dset-prototype-pollution` framework identity with CWE-1321. Require the nearest runtime `dset` dependency and its exact official API shape: v1/v2 default ESM or CommonJS direct callable for the main entry; v3 named/aliased ESM, destructured CommonJS, namespace/CommonJS receiver, or direct `.dset` member; and no merge entry before 3.1.0. Preserve remote flow from argument one below 3.1.4, emitting `vulnerable-dset-path` or `vulnerable-dset-merge-path` according to the entry point. Preserve argument-two flow only for `dset/merge` 3.1.0/3.1.1, emitting `vulnerable-dset-merge-value`. Fresh declaration-consistent npm v2/v3 lock resolutions use corresponding `lock-resolved-*` provenance. Same-file resolution is deliberately strict: if no modeled source reaches a retained path/value expression, the model cannot fall back to another request expression on the call line. Cross-file wrapper summaries retain the exact parameter position and sink kind. Reject target-only flow, value-only flow through the main entry, repaired position/version combinations, impossible export shapes, wrong packages/members, reassigned bindings or receiver members, wrapper shadowing, absent sources, development-only declarations, lockfile-free ranges, inconsistent/v1 locks, and unsafe metadata. A 64-candidate package-local bound retains a valid sink after forty unrelated calls without activating unrelated files.

**Impact boundary.** The deterministic inventory identifies a package/API/version/position-correct primitive, not an automatic final vulnerability. For path flow, final review must prove attacker control over the runtime segment type and a nested array or other coercible dangerous key that reaches a security-relevant prototype. For merge-value flow, review must additionally prove a pre-existing object at the destination path; assignment into an absent property is not equivalent to recursive merging into an inherited prototype. Both paths require parser preservation, `Object.prototype` or another meaningful prototype mutation, a fresh-object inherited effect, cleanup and process-lifetime analysis, application error handling, and concrete authorization, execution, disclosure, integrity, availability, or other security impact. The 2.1.0 ordinary-string guard, 3.1.2 merge-key guard, and 3.1.4 pre-comparison coercion are strong counterevidence for their exact repaired primitives.

## 2026-08-07 — Extend jsonpath-plus RCE coverage through the later 10.4.0 repair

**Primary evidence and beyond-parity boundary.** GitHub's reviewed critical GHSA-pppg-cpfq-h7wr / CVE-2024-21534 marks `jsonpath-plus` releases before 10.2.0 affected by remote code execution, and reviewed GHSA-hw8r-x6gr-5gjp / CVE-2025-1302 extends the vulnerable set through releases before 10.3.0 ([first reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-pppg-cpfq-h7wr), [second reviewed advisory](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hw8r-x6gr-5gjp)). Upstream subsequently released 10.4.0 specifically for another safe-evaluator RCE bypass: the repair blocks `__lookupGetter__` and `__lookupSetter__` prototype properties and restores rejection when expression evaluation recovers the `Function` constructor ([upstream repair `1bab1cc`](https://github.com/JSONPath-Plus/JSONPath/commit/1bab1cc), [official API and evaluator modes](https://github.com/JSONPath-Plus/JSONPath)). Isolated live installs confirm the non-destructive path `$[?(@root.toString.__lookupGetter__("__proto__").call(@root.toString).constructor("return process.version")())]` executes under 10.3.0 and is rejected at accessor lookup under 10.4.0. The scanner therefore follows the complete executable upstream boundary below 10.4.0 instead of stopping at the reviewed-advisory cutoff.

**Decision and precision contract.** Add a separate `node-http-jsonpath-plus-code-injection` identity with CWE-94. Require the exact `jsonpath-plus` module and an official named/aliased ESM or destructured CommonJS `JSONPath` binding, namespace or CommonJS receiver, or direct `require("jsonpath-plus").JSONPath` member. Preserve remote flow only from the options object's `path` property or the documented positional path argument; request data used only as the JSON document is outside the model. Default, `true`, `undefined`, and explicit `safe` evaluation require nearest runtime proof below 10.4.0 from either an exact production/optional declaration or a declaration-consistent adjacent npm v2/v3 lock. Emit distinct `vulnerable-jsonpath-plus-safe-eval` and `lock-resolved-vulnerable-jsonpath-plus-safe-eval` provenance. Explicit `eval: "native"` is intentionally version-independent because the documented mode delegates expressions to native evaluation; emit `jsonpath-plus-native-eval` even at a patched package version. Explicit `eval: false` is strong counterevidence. Reject an unproved custom evaluator, 10.4.0+ safe mode, unsupported default imports or wrong members, wrong-package metadata, binding/receiver/member reassignment, wrapper shadowing, lockfile-free ranges for safe mode, development-only declarations, inconsistent or v1 locks, and unsafe metadata.

**Impact boundary.** Deterministic inventory records a high-confidence expression-to-evaluator path; the final reviewer must still prove accepted JSONPath expression grammar, recovery of an executable constructor or equivalent native evaluation, process/global access, application error handling, sandbox and privilege boundaries, and a concrete execution, credential, filesystem, network, disclosure, integrity, or availability effect. Advisory membership alone is not final exploit proof. Conversely, `safe` is not accepted as a control below 10.4.0, and package upgrade is not accepted as a control when the application explicitly selects `native` evaluation.

**Performance correction.** The broad documented callable forms require inspecting aliased direct calls in package-activated files, so the model retains the existing package-local 64-candidate ceiling and proves a real sink after forty unrelated calls. The initial whole-repository regression exposed repeated nearest-manifest traversal for each candidate, taking 54.49 seconds on Windows. Cache `nodeRuntimeDependency` results, including negative results, in a `WeakMap` keyed by the immutable inventory snapshot and a source-path/package pair. The cache cannot survive or contaminate another inventory; every package identity and lock check remains isolated. The same regression falls to 13.99 seconds, and the existing `js-toml` repository-retention path remains green at 14.04 seconds. This is a general performance improvement for all exact package-aware models without changing trust or version semantics.
