## 2026-08-06 — Separate Mongoose update grammar from selectors

**Decision.** Add `node-http-mongoose-update` as a distinct host model instead of broadening `node-http-mongoose-nosql`. A candidate must resolve the same exact official Mongoose factory and unique non-reassigned Model identity, prove execution, and place request-derived data in the documented update argument of Model `updateOne`, `updateMany`, `findOneAndUpdate`, or `findByIdAndUpdate`. Operator or query-grammar control is classified as CWE-943; unintended attacker-selected fields without grammar control are classified as CWE-915. The deterministic row carries both IDs so the model reviewer must choose the concrete runtime effect.

**Why.** MongoDB accepts either an update-operator document or an aggregation pipeline in the update position, and operators including `$set`, `$unset`, `$rename`, and `$inc` change write semantics rather than acting as inert data ([MongoDB `updateOne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.updateone/), [MongoDB update operators](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/update/), [MongoDB `$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/update/unset/)). Mongoose documents the Model methods as filter, update, and options positions; it also treats top-level non-operator update keys as `$set` while update pipelines are not cast ([Mongoose Model API](https://mongoosejs.com/docs/api/model.html)). Consequently, the selector model cannot safely infer this flow from argument zero, and a method-name-only matcher would confuse filters, options, replacement APIs, and query-chain overloads. CodeQL exposes `nosql-injection` as a dedicated JavaScript sink kind, supporting query-language classification when the attacker controls update grammar ([CodeQL custom JavaScript library models](https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/customizing-library-models-for-javascript/)). CWE-915 remains the more exact classification when only unauthorized object attributes are writable.

**Exact position and consumption.** Reuse the official default, namespace, named `model`, and CommonJS binding proof from the selector model. The Model declaration must precede the sink, both factory and Model must remain unmodified, and a wrapper parameter cannot masquerade as the Model. Extract only argument one and require `await`, `exec`, `then`, `catch`, or return from an async exported wrapper. Deliberately reject replacement APIs and one-argument calls. A query-chain `Query#findOneAndUpdate(update)` has a different argument position and remains outside this exact Model model until its receiver identity and overload can be proved independently.

**Counterevidence.** Retain `fixed-update-field-value-boundary` only when every tainted wrapper parameter occurs as the scalar value of a fixed literal field beneath a server-owned `$set` object. A complete request object beneath `$set`, computed field, spread, tainted data outside that `$set`, denylist, or same-named helper does not qualify. `mongoose.sanitizeFilter` governs filters rather than updates. Mongoose update validators are disabled by default and, even when `runValidators` is enabled, apply only to selected operators and updated paths; `$inc` is among the documented exceptions ([Mongoose validation](https://mongoosejs.com/docs/validation.html#update-validators)). Casting, strict mode, middleware, authentication, and `requireFilter` therefore remain review leads rather than universal update grammar or field-authorization controls.

**Red/green boundary.** The strict red run passed only the manifest shape and failed the other four tests because no update row or reviewer guidance existed. After implementation and ranking hardening, 6 tests and 32 assertions pass. The four official binding/operation positives are the only rows in the position matrix; filter-only, options-only, replacement, one-argument, lookalike, and inert cases emit none. All five adversarial control cases remain reviewable, but only the fixed `$set` field receives counterevidence. The real positive preserves nine ordered relative-import/call/parameter propagators to `src/storage.js:12` with no candidate control; the matched control retains the same row and adds only the fixed-field boundary. Its witnesses prove that `{ $unset: { mfaSecret: 1 } }` removes the MFA secret in the vulnerable path and cannot cross the fixed-field path.

**Whole-repository prioritization boundary.** The first compiled self-review was deterministic and fast but retained only the safe update fixture at the global 96-row cap. Because that row sorted first and contributed the unique fixed-control category, category seeding selected it while the otherwise identical dangerous category was already represented. That acceptance result was rejected. Equal-priority records carrying `fixed-update-field-value-boundary` now sort behind a matching unmitigated record; category diversity still retains the controlled twin, so both review and counterevidence survive. A first general rule that ranked every record by candidate-control count was also rejected: the authoritative suite exposed three deterministic ordering changes in GORM expression/clause rows, pgconn query/COPY rows, and Java static `Path` factory specializations. Those candidate controls include binding and incomplete-risk evidence rather than established mitigation. The final comparator recognizes only the exact fixed update boundary, and a dedicated adversarial regression places a lexically earlier controlled file against a later dangerous file. The adjacent update, saturation, GORM, pgconn, and Java path matrix passes 135 tests and 1,438 assertions with one intentional symlink skip.

**Acceptance evidence.** The authoritative suite passes 1,160 tests and 8,769 assertions across 123 files with 19 intentional environment/platform skips and no failures. The clean production build emits 96 byte-identical self-inventory rows in 13,254 and 12,407 ms with SHA-256 `1b21c3c5a9e770db2b337bf520d53f9868324333a77ffa1f7c14aff23a66139e`; the unmitigated update row precedes the controlled twin, and no other update row appears. Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript checking, and the production advisory audit pass with no known vulnerabilities. Strict package inspection validates 251 entries, and three isolated Windows/Linux installs validate public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled plugin files. The final local tarball is 1,544,434 bytes with SHA-1 `40971c8d3ee856702930ac3435ee4d20fbaa05f2` and SHA-256 `6a1015d85f026efca7044d49476d968a16ef5bff1faef5c15439bf46c829af27` before removal. The first local checker invocation deliberately failed only because release-only `gitHead` enforcement was mistakenly enabled against a local package that correctly omits release provenance; the ordinary local contract and all three installs passed. Windows builds with zero warnings/errors, passes seven core and three shared tests, and publishes a 346,796-byte executable with SHA-256 `921e75e15d360df15fe0d84d81cce14580d24523fd4eebf7cdc343558d3a7309`. WSL Ubuntu performs locked restores under a Linux-only `PATH`, builds with zero warnings/errors, passes seven core, three shared, and two headless Linux tests, and passes non-graphical plus X11/Xvfb startup. Its 72,568-byte executable has SHA-256 `53c4e49e6f0aecdafec913a4d5b2423d70503f35db12c5228c0e25768fc6421d`.

**Consequence.** Selector and update semantics can evolve independently without position confusion, and the reviewer receives explicit obligations for document selection, tenant/object authorization, sensitive fields, upserts, validators, middleware, immutable and discriminator keys, pipeline behavior, write outcome, and database authority. The bounded model intentionally misses query-chain overloads, bulk-write operation arrays, replacement-document over-posting, aggregation stages assembled through helpers, dynamically selected Model methods, and flows beyond three import boundaries. Those need their own exact receiver/position contracts rather than relaxation of this model.

## 2026-08-06 — Model exact Mongoose selector injection

**Decision.** Add a standalone `node-http-mongoose-nosql` host model for document-selector injection rather than relying on the residual prompt's generic NoSQL co-occurrence search. A candidate must resolve an official `mongoose` binding, prove that a unique local Model was constructed through the exact still-unmodified binding, place a request-derived value in the documented filter argument of a supported Model query, and prove that the query is consumed. Classify the broken data/query-grammar boundary as CWE-943.

**Why.** MongoDB filter objects are executable query structure, not merely scalar values: an object such as `{ $ne: null }` changes selection semantics. CodeQL's JavaScript query help explicitly treats object-valued NoSQL input as query-language injection and recommends either an exact primitive/literal boundary or `$eq` around untrusted values ([CodeQL JavaScript database-query injection](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/javascript/js-sql-injection/)). CodeQL's extensible JavaScript library models expose a dedicated `nosql-injection` sink kind and exact argument positions, and its standard library models cover MongoDB and Mongoose query objects ([custom JavaScript library models](https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/customizing-library-models-for-javascript/), [CodeQL JavaScript library](https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/codeql-library-for-javascript/)). Mongoose documents Model queries separately from their update, projection, and options arguments, while MongoDB's Node driver describes `findOne` as selecting the first document matching its query filter ([Mongoose Model API](https://mongoosejs.com/docs/api/model.html), [MongoDB `findOne`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/v6.13/usage-examples/findOne/)). A method-name-only match would therefore overtaint update bodies and unrelated objects while missing the semantic operator boundary.

**Identity, position, and execution proof.** Accept default and namespace ESM receivers, whole-module CommonJS receivers, and named ESM/CommonJS `model` aliases. A receiver form must call its exact `.model(...)` member; a named function form must be invoked directly. The factory declaration must precede the model, cannot be reassigned before construction, and the resulting model name must be unique, cannot be a wrapper parameter, and cannot be reassigned before the sink. Only argument zero is extracted from `countDocuments`, `deleteMany`, `deleteOne`, `exists`, `find`, `findOne`, `findOneAndDelete`, `findOneAndReplace`, `findOneAndUpdate`, `replaceOne`, `updateMany`, and `updateOne`. The existing bounded Node summary graph then preserves that exact filter expression through as many as three relative-import call/parameter boundaries. A query is eligible only when the sink line awaits it, explicitly consumes it through `exec`, `then`, or `catch`, or returns the thenable from an async exported wrapper. A bare return from a synchronous wrapper is inert and rejected.

**Counterevidence.** An exact `$eq` boundary around the request-derived selector value is retained as `literal-query-value-equality`. An exact `mongoose.sanitizeFilter(...)` call through the proven official receiver is retained as `mongoose-filter-sanitization`; a same-named local helper is deliberately not trusted. Mongoose documents `sanitizeFilter` as wrapping nested properties whose names begin with `$` in `$eq` and exposes the option as opt-in rather than a universal default ([Mongoose API](<https://mongoosejs.com/docs/api/mongoose.html#Mongoose.prototype.sanitizeFilter()>)). The quality gate therefore requires the control to dominate the same complete filter and every effective query path. Casting, `strictQuery`, `runValidators`, `requireFilter`, authentication, projection, and result limiting do not independently establish a literal-value boundary.

**Adversarial and executable evidence.** The strict pair uses Express route → gateway → service → storage and requires all nine ordered import/call/parameter propagators. Its vulnerable storage query places the request value directly under `username`; the witness evaluates a representative `$ne` selector and selects the administrator record. The matched control changes only the selector boundary to `$eq`; its witness rejects the operator object and retains literal `guest` lookup. Synthetic cases accept default, namespace, named-alias, and CommonJS model construction while excluding data confined to update or options positions, local Model lookalikes, calling the Mongoose receiver without `.model`, reassigned factories, synchronous inert returned queries, and local sanitizer lookalikes. The first red run retained the strict manifest but emitted no exact framework rows and lacked the quality-gate instruction; the implemented model then passed all focused expectations without relaxing a gate.

**Performance correction.** The first compiled double self-review was deterministic but took 33,966 and 32,009 ms, outside the preceding scanner's 19–22 second envelope. A CPU profile attributed most samples to repeated JavaScript comment/string masking, structural-line construction, and exported-wrapper discovery. The graph was recalculating the same immutable source snapshot across same-file, terminal-wrapper, and relay stages, and exported JavaScript discovery separately remasked a thirteen-line slice for every source line. The corrected implementation materializes one structural array per snapshot and weakly caches JavaScript code lines, JavaScript/Python structural lines, and exported JavaScript/Python wrapper summaries. Weak keys bind every value to the exact immutable line-array identity and permit the complete source snapshot to be collected after a scan; no cache crosses changed source bytes. The final compiled pair takes 12,424 and 12,271 ms, about 2.7 times faster than the rejected build and materially faster than the previous envelope, while retaining 96 byte-identical rows and SHA-256 `73cdbd3b376a4866ff6c119f6370a64908def3adb8c7f7656675a0ed99ed4fee`.

**Acceptance evidence.** The strengthened focused lane passes 5 tests and 31 assertions, the residual-inventory lane passes 65 tests and 1,052 assertions with one intentional symlink skip, and both executable witnesses pass. The authoritative optimized suite passes 1,154 tests and 8,737 assertions across 122 files with 19 intentional environment/platform skips and no failures. Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript checking, the clean production build, and the production advisory audit pass with no known vulnerabilities. Repeated compiled self-review contains only the two expected Mongoose benchmark-fixture hypotheses. Strict package inspection validates 251 entries; three isolated Windows/Linux installs validate public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled plugin files. The removed 1,541,238-byte archive had SHA-1 `4b82e1f13fb7055e7038fe559d82e701c27b16a3` and SHA-256 `1de79f567bf8586c1e5cc67adf8777bff835775b13682c65e22c6e76ed94ba34`. Windows builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core and three shared desktop tests, and publishes a 346,796-byte executable with SHA-256 `aa14cc0e68a317cdf4b6b8c7e0ce4244464f307a5fbf7ee0464a0b045c685372`. WSL Ubuntu performs locked restores, builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core, three shared, and two Linux interface tests, and passes non-graphical plus X11/Xvfb startup. Its 72,568-byte executable has SHA-256 `53c4e49e6f0aecdafec913a4d5b2423d70503f35db12c5228c0e25768fc6421d`.

**Failure boundary.** Arbitrary Mongoose re-exports, discriminators, dynamically selected or computed Model names, query-helper plugins, aggregate pipelines, `bulkWrite`, update-operator and field-name injection, compiler-resolved aliases beyond the accepted binding forms, callback-only execution, and runtime monkey patching remain outside this exact host proof. The broad residual search and mandatory model correction pass still receive those surfaces. Any future expansion must add an API-specific argument contract, an execution boundary, and paired exploit/control evidence rather than broadening the method regex alone.

## 2026-08-06 — Model exact Node and Python filesystem path positions

**Decision.** Add standalone `node-http-path` and `python-web-path` host models that resolve official filesystem bindings before tracing data and that attach taint only to each API's documented path-bearing arguments. Preserve the existing three-boundary relative-import graph, but do not let an operation-name regex establish ownership. For Node, accept named ESM and CommonJS aliases, namespace and default ESM receivers, CommonJS receivers/destructuring, promises variants, and direct official `require` receivers. For Python, accept an unshadowed builtin `open`, exact `builtins`, `os`, and `shutil` module aliases, and exact named aliases. Reject foreign modules, local lookalikes, parameter shadows, and binding reassignment.

**Why.** CodeQL's JavaScript and Python path-injection queries treat attacker-controlled filesystem paths as CWE-22-family risks spanning unauthorized reads, writes, and deletes ([JavaScript path injection](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/javascript/js-path-injection/), [Python path injection](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-query-help/python/py-path-injection/)). Its JavaScript library-model format also identifies the precise input position of a path-injection sink rather than assigning taint to an entire call ([JavaScript library models](https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/customizing-library-models-for-javascript/)). Node documents the `path` or `filename` position of its filesystem operations and gives copy/rename/link-like calls distinct source and destination paths ([Node filesystem API](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html)); Python similarly defines the first `open(file, ...)` argument as the path-like object and gives `shutil.copyfile(src, dst)` two path roles ([Python `open`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#open), [Python `shutil`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/shutil.html)). Whole-call taint would therefore create an avoidable false positive whenever request data is only file contents, flags, mode, options, callback data, or encoding.

**Exact binding and position proof.** A candidate line is materialized only after the host resolves one supported operation through one official binding and extracts every documented path position available at that call. Node single-path operations use argument zero; copy, cp, link, rename, and symlink families use arguments zero and one. Python builtin `open` uses argument zero; supported `os` operations use their documented one- or two-path shape; `shutil` copy/move families use source and destination, while `rmtree` uses its first path. Dynamic alias calls are discovered from the resolved imports rather than from operation spelling alone. Binding declarations must precede the call, must not be replaced before it, and must not be shadowed by the containing exported wrapper parameter. The exact extracted expressions—not the complete call—drive same-file source matching and wrapper-parameter summaries. Bounded initializer recovery preserves a fixed-map selection such as `selected = DOCUMENTS[key]` or `DOCUMENTS.get(key)` through the terminal wrapper.

**Containment and counterevidence.** A server-owned key mapped to one fixed complete path is strong counterevidence and may be declared at module scope. Mere canonicalization or absolute-path rejection is not emitted as a standalone control lead unless component-aware containment is also present. Node documents lexical path operations separately from filesystem access ([Node path API](https://nodejs.org/api/path.html)); Python warns that `os.path.commonprefix` can return invalid paths and directs callers needing component-aware comparison to `commonpath` ([Python `os.path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/os.path.html#os.path.commonprefix)). `path.resolve`, `os.path.join`, `normpath`, `abspath`, `realpath`, and `Path.resolve` remain construction or canonicalization evidence, not universal authorization: later absolute segments can reset an intended base, and lexical reasoning does not close symbolic-link, junction, mount, hard-link, writable-ancestor, or rename-race behavior. The quality gate must separately establish exact pre-sink dominance, decoding and separator behavior, volume syntax and case folding, tenant/object authorization, permissions, and the concrete read, disclosure, create, overwrite, delete, move, link, metadata, or served-content effect.

**Adversarial and executable evidence.** The strict lane contains two four-file positives and their topology-matched fixed-map controls. The Node positive reaches exact `node:fs/promises` `readFile`; the Python positive reaches the unshadowed builtin `open`; both carry the request through route, gateway, service, and storage and record three imports, calls, and parameters. Synthetic cases accept five Node binding shapes and five Python binding shapes, including taint in copy destination position, while rejecting request-controlled `writeFile` content, local Node lookalikes, a local Python `open`, and a foreign imported `open`. The regression also requires an official FastAPI import before `Path(...)` can be treated as a FastAPI-bound request source, preventing `pathlib.Path(...)` from creating a same-file duplicate. Real Node and WSL Ubuntu Python witnesses read their private parent fixture in each vulnerable case; both controls reject the traversal key and retain the public `welcome` read.

**Performance correction.** The red-to-green implementation initially invoked full binding and exported-wrapper discovery from every call-bearing line. That preserved correctness on fixtures but made a compiled inventory of the SDK take roughly 70–75 seconds per pass and caused the first double self-scan to exceed its three-minute command bound. Acceptance rejected that implementation. The final design first admits only lines containing a supported operation or an exact official named alias, then caches immutable Node binding/wrapper context in a `WeakMap` keyed by the source-line array. The cache neither crosses source snapshots nor retains them after the inventory graph is released. The same compiled self-scan now takes 22,257 ms and 19,425 ms for consecutive passes—about a threefold reduction—while producing the same 96 rows, zero Node/Python filesystem-path rows, byte equality, and SHA-256 `23822919ec67fc4302c030d55a29c3097227139b11fdc91fadbb84d73f26e249`.

**Acceptance evidence.** The focused lane passes 5 tests and 32 assertions. The authoritative post-cache suite passes 1,149 tests and 8,706 assertions across 121 files with 19 intentional environment/integration skips and no failures. Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript checking, and the clean production build pass. The pnpm production advisory audit reports no known vulnerabilities. Strict package inspection validates 251 entries; three isolated Windows/Linux installs validate public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled plugin files. The removed 1,518,640-byte archive had SHA-1 `f328aa0a1b2bf2ed5173c833e51dcfabed7bd2e4` and SHA-256 `3260a0e7faa4d616ec78982371af383cd106c1f1be9d1050efc6488861b84040`.

**Failure boundary.** Runtime monkey patching, computed property names, arbitrary re-exports, star or dot imports, Python keyword-only remapping, callbacks, custom filesystem wrappers, file-descriptor provenance, archive extraction, upload placement, and full filesystem race/link resolution remain outside this exact host proof. Unsupported or ambiguous binding syntax suppresses only the deterministic framework record; the model still receives the broader residual search and must validate any independently discovered path risk. Future expansion should add paired exploit/control evidence and an exact binding/argument contract rather than widening the operation-name regex.

## 2026-08-06 — Compose three exact Node and Python import boundaries

**Decision.** Extend the Node/TypeScript and Python framework summary graph from one relay layer to a hard maximum of two relay layers before the terminal sink wrapper. A request source may therefore preserve one value through as many as three exact call/parameter boundaries. Build the graph iteratively from terminal wrappers, retain both relay depths for callers, and emit every import, call argument, and wrapper parameter in source-to-sink order.

**Why.** Route/gateway/service/wrapper layouts are common and the existing host already had exact repository-relative resolution, exported-symbol discovery, positional parameter binding, reassignment rejection, and language-aware masking. The old one-relay ceiling therefore dropped an otherwise fully proved outer gateway. CodeQL distinguishes local from global interprocedural flow and uses summaries to synthesize flow through calls ([data-flow analysis](https://codeql.github.com/docs/writing-codeql-queries/about-data-flow-analysis/)). Node defines relative ESM specifiers as paths relative to the importing file and requires explicit file extensions ([Node ESM import specifiers](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#import-specifiers)); Python gives leading-dot imports package-relative meaning ([Python import system](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/import.html#package-relative-imports)). Those exact syntactic boundaries support one additional deterministic composition layer without accepting bare Node packages, ambiguous absolute Python imports, re-export inference, or runtime loader behavior.

**Bounded graph proof.** Start with existing sink wrappers, derive one relay layer from them, then derive one more layer only from the first. Each Node edge must resolve through the existing repository-relative ESM/CommonJS resolver to the exact imported export. Each Python edge must remain an explicit relative `from` import resolving to one public module-level function. At every layer, bind the exact positional argument to the exact exported parameter, require the call to remain inside that wrapper, and reject parameter reassignment before the call. Chain materialization rejects repeated source paths or malformed recursion and cannot exceed two relay nodes. Controls are collected from every relay and the terminal wrapper; the record key includes every relay file, call line, and parameter position so distinct exact paths do not collide.

**Adversarial and regression evidence.** The strict Node and Python command/SQL exploit-control fixtures now use route → gateway → service → sink-wrapper topologies. The red baseline lost exactly the two vulnerable command expectations and retained all existing safe behavior. After composition, each vulnerable command and SQL case emits one model with three imports, three calls, three parameters, and no duplicate path; both parameterized-SQL controls retain their exact binding lead, while both shell-free command controls remain outside the dangerous sink model. Synthetic controls reject reassignment in the newly added outer gateway, a deliberately over-depth route → gateway → facade → service → wrapper path, and a repeated-file service/runner cycle in both languages. Seven focused tests pass 59 assertions.

**Failure boundary.** A fourth import hop, Node package exports and loader hooks, dynamic imports, Python absolute imports, re-exports, star imports, keyword remapping, decorators, monkey patching, callbacks, transformed values, and runtime dispatch remain unsupported. Ambiguity, reassignment at any relay, repeated files, or an over-depth chain suppresses only that composed multi-hop record. Extending the cap again requires measured false-negative evidence plus paired cycle, ambiguity, reassignment, and performance controls.

**Acceptance evidence.** The widened Node/Python framework and residual-inventory matrix passes 122 tests and 1,409 assertions with one intentional platform skip. The authoritative Windows suite passes 1,144 tests and 8,674 assertions across 120 files with 19 intentional environment/integration skips and no failures. Compiled self-review emits 96 byte-identical rows across repeated runs with SHA-256 `58e405b01f27bcad52e3155b87f76451d69d54536c08da064d5b8297de1a11bd`. Each vulnerable command and SQL fixture emits exactly one three-boundary model with nine ordered propagators; both shell-free command controls emit no dangerous model, and each parameterized SQL control retains one exact binding lead. Node syntax checks and its live SQLite grammar/binding witness pass. WSL Python syntax checks and the live SQLite exploit/control witness pass under an isolated bytecode cache.

Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript checking, the clean production build, and the production advisory audit pass with no known vulnerabilities. Strict package inspection validates 251 entries; three isolated Windows/Linux installations validate public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled plugin files. The Linux package probe initially used Ubuntu's unsupported `/usr/bin/node` 18.19.1 and failed on the Node 22 `node:zlib` `crc32` export; the declared and installed `/usr/local/bin/node` 22.23.1 passed without weakening the engine contract. The removed 1,522,403-byte archive had SHA-1 `444816fbfd4e8dbce2821e28b6125cfab0aedb4d` and SHA-256 `8cfc4b83f459af9b313950968a8aacc4374805177065581dd7af40ff88894960`. Windows builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core and three shared desktop tests, and publishes a 346,796-byte executable with SHA-256 `40cd6f979a159568b44b875c7c59d1a3b867fe530b2a8350918288a2023dac52`. WSL Ubuntu performs locked restores under a Linux-only path, builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core, three shared, and two Linux interface tests, and passes non-graphical plus X11/Xvfb startup. Its 72,568-byte executable has SHA-256 `53c4e49e6f0aecdafec913a4d5b2423d70503f35db12c5228c0e25768fc6421d`.

**Consequence.** Every existing Node/TypeScript and Python typed sink family gains the extra exact gateway layer without broadening source or sink recognition. All four language families now share a three-boundary host ceiling, while their language-specific identity proofs remain independent and auditable.

**Decision.** Extend the existing typed Java and C# framework summary graph from one relay layer to a hard maximum of two relay layers before the terminal sink wrapper. The record key contains every relay file, call line, and parameter position so distinct exact paths neither collide nor duplicate.

## 2026-08-06 — Resolve exact direct Maven reactor dependencies

**Decision.** Extend only the Java basename-helper visibility graph with direct conventional Maven reactor dependencies. A caller can read a sibling only when its own top-level `dependencies` block contains literal `groupId`, `artifactId`, and `version` coordinates that identify exactly one module in exactly one retained reactor; the scope is absent, `compile`, or `provided`; the type is absent or `jar`; no classifier is present; and caller plus helper both remain under conventional `src/main/java`. Preserve direction and do not make the graph transitive.

**Why.** The Maven reactor [sorts a project dependency before its consumer](https://maven.apache.org/guides/mini/guide-multiple-modules.html), but `dependencyManagement` alone does not affect that order. Maven's [dependency mechanism](https://maven.apache.org/guides/introduction/introduction-to-dependency-mechanism.html) places `compile` dependencies on the production compile classpath and `provided` dependencies on the compile and test classpaths, while `runtime` and `test` do not establish production compilation. The previous nearest-POM partition correctly rejected undeclared siblings but also lost ordinary direct helper-library calls that the compiler can resolve. Recovering only the exact declared reactor edge improves recall without returning to repository-wide name matching.

**Bounded graph proof.** Parse only a deliberately small, non-executing XML surface: one `project` with exact model version 4.0.0, its direct coordinates and optional packaging, one exact local parent, literal `modules`, and direct top-level dependencies. Reject DTDs, CDATA, entity references, prefixed or otherwise unsupported XML syntax, misplaced or duplicate XML declarations, excessive nesting, duplicate structural fields, property expressions, and unsafe repository-relative paths. A caller can read its own module plus a target module named by an exact literal `api`, `implementation`, `compileOnly`, or `compileOnlyApi` `project(":path")` declaration in the caller's own top-level `dependencies` block. **Decision.** Carry an already proven `spring-http-path` value through a same-file helper return before deriving `java-file-getname-path-boundary` or `java-path-getfilename-path-boundary`. Preserve the reduction's helper-body source line as evidence and allow the existing caller-side exact parent rejection to control the returned lineage.

**Why.** Real Java repositories routinely hide small normalization and naming operations behind local helpers. The base Spring graph already preserved the request through the helper call because the value still reached the typed filesystem sink, but both basename specializations reopened only the exported sink method and therefore missed the actual `getName` or `getFileName` expression in a private helper. That was a demonstrated false negative, not a hypothetical feature request. CodeQL likewise treats callable summaries as explicit input-to-return flow models in its [Java/Kotlin library-model documentation](https://codeql.github.com/docs/codeql-language-guides/customizing-library-models-for-java-and-kotlin/). Java method calls require owner, applicability, arity, and overload resolution under [JLS 15.12](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-15.html#jls-15.12); because this host has no compiler database, it accepts a deliberately smaller set that it can identify exactly and rejects every overloaded symbol rather than guessing the most-specific declaration.

**Bounded summary proof.** Parse outer-class member methods at lexical depth one, including non-exported helpers and exact parameter/return declarations. Structurally mask comments and literals, require exactly one terminal `return`, and reject nested blocks, lambdas, branches, loops, synchronization, abrupt statements, and trailing code. Within that straight-line prefix, propagate only exact identifier aliases, exact official `new File`, `Path.of`, or `Paths.get` constructions, exact basename reductions, and their result aliases; clear every lineage on reassignment or transformation. At the call site, require exact arity and an exact identifier argument from the already proven String/File/Path lineage. Only bare, `this.`, and exact owner-type receivers are eligible. Helper-to-helper calls, arbitrary object receivers, expressions in the summarized argument, overloads, unofficial types, tests/examples, and cross-file helpers fail closed.

**Declaration identity.** The executable fixture conversion exposed that a bounded multiline declaration window could rediscover the same method from a leading blank or annotation line. Collapse only discoveries with the same symbol, normalized return type, exact parameter declarations, and structural end line, retaining the latest declaration start so reduction line accounting remains exact. Different parameter declarations remain distinct; a true overload still makes every same-name summary ineligible.

## 2026-08-05 — Require branch-local abrupt completion for Java basename rejection

**Decision.** Attach `parent-path-component-rejection` to exact `java.io.File.getName()` and `java.nio.file.Path.getFileName()` lineages only when the exact parent equality is the complete positive condition, the matching branch itself unconditionally completes through `return` or `throw`, and that guard begins in the same lexical block path as the later filesystem sink. Apply the same rule to both basename specializations and to both direct and reverse equality forms. Preserve the specialized risk row when this proof is absent.

**Why.** The prior bounded matcher found an exact equality and then searched the next four source lines for any `return` or `throw`. That could credit a logging-only parent check merely because a later, unrelated state check threw. It could also misclassify a negated equality, a condition conjoined with an optional flag, a parent check nested under an optional outer branch, or a throw caught before the sink. Java executes an `if` branch only for the corresponding Boolean result, and `return`/`throw` prevent normal completion only along the statement that actually executes; [JLS Chapter 14](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/specs/jls/se21/html/jls-14.html) defines those normal and abrupt completion rules. CodeQL exposes the stronger formulation through Java [guard-control](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-standard-libraries/java/semmle/code/java/controlflow/Guards.qll/module.Guards.html) and [dominance](https://codeql.github.com/codeql-standard-libraries/java/semmle/code/java/controlflow/Dominance.qll/module.Dominance.html) predicates. This scanner has no compiler CFG, so adjacency was too weak and a conservative lexical proof is preferable to false counterevidence.

**Bounded control proof.** Mask comments and literals structurally while retaining the original condition for exact `".."`, `Path.of("..")`, and `Paths.get("..")` identity. Assign a stable nested block path and switch-ancestor flag from structural braces. Require the candidate `if` and sink to start in the same block path outside a switch block, which rejects a guard hidden in an optional outer block, a caught throw whose sink occurs after the enclosing `try`/`catch`, and a guard in a different `case` entry from the sink. Strip only balanced outer condition parentheses and anchor the whole condition to direct or reverse equality; negation, `&&`, `||`, and unrelated predicates therefore fail closed. For an unbraced branch, require its statement to begin with `return` or `throw`. For a braced branch, allow straight-line statements ending in `return` or `throw`, but reject nested braces, branches, loops, `try`/`catch`/`finally`, `switch`, synchronization, and lambdas. Do not treat `break` or `continue` as method-level rejection. Full Java CFG, exception-type resolution, Boolean implication, finally semantics, and helper summaries remain outside this host proof.

**Adversarial and executable evidence.** The positive `Path.getFileName()` Spring fixture now compares the exact reduced value with `Path.of("..")`, logs the match, and then performs an unrelated null-state throw check before `Files.readString`. The old four-line heuristic would have attached rejection; the new proof does not. Its pure-JDK witness logs the parent request and still reads the parent `content.txt`. The unchanged matched control terminates the exact parent branch and rejects both exact and nested parent names. Both Maven fixtures compile with Java 17 release semantics on WSL Java 21 and both witnesses execute with their expected exploit/control outcomes.

**Regression evidence.** Focused tests cover direct and reverse equality, static factories, a straight-line audit followed by abrupt completion, negated equality, conditional conjunction, optional nesting, caught throws, distinct switch cases, logging-only branches, unrelated nearby throws, another reduction, post-sink checks, and both `File` and `Path` lineages; 16 tests pass 106 assertions. The widened Java cross-file, path, framework, multi-hop, and residual-risk slice passes 105 tests and 1,272 assertions with one intentional platform skip. Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript checking, and the clean production build pass. Compiled inventory emits the positive specialization at `DocumentStore.java:24` with only `incomplete-java-nio-path-getfilename-reduction`, emits the matched control at line 21 with the additional `parent-path-component-rejection`, and emits no Java basename specialization from the production SDK's 96 deterministic records.

**Acceptance evidence.** The authoritative Windows suite passes 1,132 tests and 8,614 assertions across 120 files with 19 intentional environment/integration skips and no failures. The production advisory audit reports no known vulnerabilities. Strict package inspection validates 251 entries; two isolated installations validate public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled-plugin files. The removed 1,491,884-byte archive had SHA-256 `631674a674521d3e232baa67ed108e5b587612d485fb416e8bb3f766902834cf`. Windows builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core and three shared tests, and publishes a fresh 346,796-byte executable with SHA-256 `2c0ffc204424ee15b9a226790796edf7ad9a458bde5edb4e2725fe765131660b`. WSL Ubuntu performs locked restores after the Windows publication, builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core, three shared, and two Linux interface tests, and passes non-graphical plus X11/Xvfb startup. **Consequence.** A syntactically impressive but noncontrolling check can no longer bias the model toward a false negative merely because abrupt syntax is nearby. Future work may replace the bounded lexical proof with a compiler-backed CFG and exception graph, but must preserve exact reduced-value identity, branch polarity, sink dominance, and uncaught abrupt completion.

## 2026-08-05 — Resolve Java path factories by compilation-unit identity

**Decision.** Resolve simple `Path`, `Paths`, `of`, and `get` factory names under the Java compilation unit's import and package context before deriving `java-path-getfilename-path-boundary`. Preserve exact fully qualified factories. Treat a single-type `java.nio.file.Path` or `Paths` import as authoritative over a top-level same-package declaration, but allow an on-demand `java.nio.file.*` import only when the nearest Maven project has no top-level type with the same name in that package. Accept exact and on-demand static imports of `Path.of` and `Paths.get` only when no local owner method, qualified lookalike invocation, or competing same-name static import can own the unqualified call.

**Why.** The initial exact reduction deliberately rejected local `Path`/`Paths` declarations but did not inspect another compilation unit in the same package and did not recognize static factories. The Java 21 language rules distinguish these cases: a single-type import shadows a top-level same-package type declared in another compilation unit, while an on-demand import does not shadow it. CodeQL's Java library exposes resolved reference types, declaring methods, packages, and compilation units rather than inferring ownership from method spelling. This host has no compiler database, so it now implements the relevant identity slice explicitly and fails closed where static overload ownership would require full method resolution.

**Package and type boundary.** Parse the declared package from masked structural source. Build a brace-depth-zero surface to collect only top-level class, interface, enum, record, and annotation-interface names; a nested `Path` inside another class is not a package member and does not suppress a wildcard import in a sibling compilation unit. Restrict peers to the sink file's nearest `pom.xml` project, require the same declared package, and exclude test/example paths so test-only helpers cannot hide production identities. An exact single-type import stays eligible despite a peer name. A wildcard import loses to an exact same-project, same-package peer. A different package, nested declaration, nested Maven module, or fully qualified factory does not alter the binding.

**Static method boundary.** Normalize whitespace around selectors before matching. Support `import static java.nio.file.Path.of`, `Path.*`, `Paths.get`, and `Paths.*`, including exact parent equality through the same imported factory. Extract only unqualified calls; `Evil.of(path)` cannot fall through to the simple `of` pattern. Scan the outer type's brace-depth-one member surface for a local method declaration and reject the imported name when present. Reject another explicit same-name static import or another static wildcard because signature and overload resolution are unavailable without a compiler database. Preserve request argument, receiver/result alias, reassignment, reduction-origin, sink, and parent-rejection requirements unchanged.

**Regression evidence.** Fourteen focused tests pass 90 assertions. Positive cases cover exact `Path` and `Paths`, fully qualified factories, typed parameters, same-package single-type precedence, nested and different-package lookalikes, and all four exact/on-demand static `of`/`get` import forms. Negative cases cover same-package wildcard `Path` and `Paths` shadows, same-file shadows, qualified lookalike calls, local owner methods, competing static wildcards, unrelated reductions, fixed values, reassignment, tests, and cross-file parameter mismatch. The exact statically imported `of("..")` parent guard remains attached to the same reaching reduction, and prompt regressions preserve the import-precedence and static-owner boundary for the model reviewer.

**Acceptance evidence.** The widened Java, Spring, framework, and residual-risk slice passes 124 tests and 1,344 assertions with one intentional platform skip. The authoritative suite passes 1,130 tests and 8,598 assertions across 120 files with 19 intentional environment/integration skips and no failures. Compiled review preserves the exact positive specialization with only the incomplete-reduction lead, the exact control specialization with parent rejection, and zero specializations from the production SDK's 96 deterministic rows. Formatting, generated-model drift, TypeScript checking, the clean production build, and the production advisory audit pass. Strict package inspection validates 251 entries; two isolated installations validate public import, CLI behavior, and all 79 bundled-plugin files. The removed 1,488,545-byte archive had SHA-256 `685125d6820580614843fc2085ae86626eede0e0642a7d2bebf24b6e9d4e8ca3`. Windows builds without warnings/errors, passes seven core and three shared tests, and publishes a 346,796-byte executable with SHA-256 `31a2439db5e1994f5c1b006c6accc7048aeef3d3a06507cf5786683de282a296`. WSL Ubuntu builds without warnings/errors; passes seven core, three shared, and two headless tests; and passes non-graphical plus X11/Xvfb startup. Its 72,568-byte executable has SHA-256 `53c4e49e6f0aecdafec913a4d5b2423d70503f35db12c5228c0e25768fc6421d`. A first Linux no-restore probe correctly failed after the Windows publish rewrote shared `obj` assets to Windows NuGet cache paths; repeating the locked Linux restores regenerated the platform-specific graph and the unchanged source then passed every Linux gate. **Consequence.** The scanner gains static-import recall and removes a repository-wide wildcard-import false-positive class without treating every matching filename as a shadow. Full overload resolution, module-path dependencies, annotation processors, generated sources, non-Maven source sets, static-import signature compatibility, and compiler-error recovery remain outside this bounded host model and must continue to fail closed rather than be guessed.

## 2026-08-05 — Keep exact `Path.getFileName()` parent names tainted

**Decision.** Derive `java-path-getfilename-path-boundary` only from an existing typed `spring-http-path` record. Preserve the base Spring path row because lexical basename reduction does not answer link, race, platform, deployment, tenant, object-authorization, or concrete-effect questions.

**Why.** CodeQL 2.26.2 corrected `java.io.File.getName()` because the exact input `..` survives basename reduction, but the same release does not describe `Path.getFileName`. Oracle's [`Path.getFileName` contract](<https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.base/java/nio/file/Path.html#getFileName()>) defines the result as the farthest lexical name element; it does not normalize special parent names. The executable JDK witness proves `Path.of("..").getFileName().equals(Path.of(".."))` and then reads a parent `content.txt` when that result is resolved under a trusted root. The prior generic Java model nevertheless recorded any `getFileName()` or `getNameCount()` occurrence as `single-path-component-validation`. That evidence was unsound: a one-element path can be exactly `..`, so the label could bias the model toward a false negative.

**Identity and flow boundary.** Accept simple `Path.of` only with an exact `java.nio.file.Path` or wildcard import and no local `Path` declaration. A String flow must reach the exact factory argument before its returned `Path` can become a receiver. Follow only exact receiver aliases, direct factory reductions, receiver reductions, and result aliases; clear receiver and result identity on reassignment. For cross-file rows, restrict the specialization to the final wrapper parameter already proven by the Spring graph. A fixed factory beside a separately tainted sink expression, another object's `getFileName`, the wrong parameter in a multi-parameter wrapper, local lookalikes, tests, comments, strings, and cleared values fail closed.

**Control boundary.** Remove the generic single-component candidate entirely. Record `incomplete-java-nio-path-getfilename-reduction` whenever the exact reduced lineage reaches the sink. Record `parent-path-component-rejection` only when that same lineage is compared by `Path.equals` with exact official `Path.of("..")` or `Paths.get("..")` before the sink and a bounded branch returns or throws. Preserve origin lineage through candidate-path aliases so a guard on the reduced basename still applies when the sink consumes a later resolved candidate, but do not transfer a guard from a parallel reduction with a different origin. Substring checks, logging, another variable, or a post-operation check are not counterevidence. The matched control retains identical topology and sink while comparing the same reduced `Path` with `Path.of("..")` before the operation; its witness rejects both `..` and `nested/..` and preserves `guide`. Both Maven fixtures compile against Spring Web MVC 7.0.8 with Java 17 release semantics and Maven Compiler Plugin 3.15.0; both witnesses execute on WSL Java 21. Focused regressions cover imported `Path`, imported `Paths`, fully qualified factories, typed `Path` parameters, receiver aliases, direct reductions, exact and reverse equality, origin-specific controls, weak/other/post-sink checks, local lookalikes, fixed values, reassignment, test exclusion, cross-file parameter identity, prompt guidance, and the six-case manifest. **Acceptance evidence.** The widened Java, Spring, framework, and residual-risk lane passes 122 tests and 1,337 assertions with one intentional platform skip. The authoritative Windows suite passes 1,128 tests and 8,591 assertions across 120 files with 19 intentional environment/integration skips and no failures. Compiled review emits one exact six-propagator specialization at the positive sink with only `incomplete-java-nio-path-getfilename-reduction`, the same exact path at the control sink with the additional `parent-path-component-rejection`, and no specialization from the production SDK's 96 deterministic records. It completes both runs with one expected high-severity CWE-22 finding, one true positive, no false positives or misses, and perfect completion, precision, recall, F1, case, negative-control, stability, validation, attack-path, code-evidence, and severity metrics. ## 2026-08-05 — Serialize benchmark results with an auditable runner lock

**Decision.** Acquire one exclusive `.benchmark-runner.lock` inside the external results directory before reading or creating campaign identity, resuming attempts, invoking scanners, finalizing receipts, or replacing evaluation artifacts. The versioned JSON owner record contains only the process ID, a random 128-bit ownership token, and start time. A live owner rejects a second runner immediately. Normal release and the synchronous process-exit fallback remove the path only when its complete bytes still match the caller's token-bound record.

**Why.** The authenticated Java `File.getName()` campaign exposed a boundary that per-attempt staging could not solve. The first shell host reached its 20-minute deadline while the benchmark process tree survived and began another attempt. An identical resume command then ran concurrently in the same results directory. The scanners produced the expected one positive and zero safe findings, and evaluation passed every substantive gate, but the two runners eventually collided while promoting their private staging directories into the same canonical `run-1` paths. A shell or CI timeout is not proof that its descendants stopped. Preserving partial attempts prevents destructive retry within one runner; it does not make two independent writers safe.

**Recovery and failure boundary.** Exclusive creation is the ownership primitive. If the path exists, parse at most 16 KiB from a regular non-symbolic file and probe the recorded PID with signal zero. An alive or permission-protected PID remains active, including the conservative PID-reuse case. A dead owner's bytes must remain identical across a bounded recovery delay before the file is renamed intact under `.benchmark-runner-locks/`; acquisition then retries with a fresh token and verifies that it still owns the canonical path after competing stale inspections can settle. Malformed JSON, an unknown schema, invalid PID/token/time, oversize content, a symlink, a permission failure, or excessive ownership transitions fails closed. Recovery never overwrites canonical scan output and never treats an arbitrary pre-existing results entry as operational metadata.

**Campaign and regression evidence.** Campaign `d44245ae29499c3874b2427d72eda02de31f637301c23a21d77ed23e65ea8bdd` completed two selected runs with one expected finding, one true positive, no false positives or misses, and perfect completion, precision, recall, F1, case, negative-control, stability, validation, attack-path, code-evidence, and severity metrics. The positive required one fresh model session after a model-turn deadline and completed with substantive evidence; the safe control emitted no finding. Stored GitHub authentication succeeded throughout, with no allowance, credit, rate-limit, authentication, or classifier error. The runner's eventual nonzero status came only from the orphan/resume output collision. Focused tests now prove active-owner refusal before campaign mutation, dead-owner archival followed by campaign creation, malformed-lock retention, archive-directory lookalike rejection, token-bound release, ordinary reacquisition, SARIF seed propagation, and interrupted-run finalization; 20 tests pass with 110 assertions. The authoritative Windows suite passes 1,125 tests with 19 intentional skips, no failures, and 8,562 assertions across 120 files. Formatting, generated models, types, clean build, production audit, strict 251-entry package inspection, two isolated installs, public import, CLI, and all 79 bundled files pass; the archive is removed after hashing. Windows and WSL Linux GUI build, core/shared/headless tests, publish, non-graphical startup, and X11/Xvfb startup pass.

**Consequence.** Resuming an apparently timed-out campaign can no longer spend duplicate model time or corrupt promotion merely because the original process tree outlived its host. A stale record remains auditable instead of disappearing, and unverifiable ownership requires operator inspection rather than optimistic deletion. Future work should add an explicit heartbeat or native advisory-lock backend where runtimes provide one, externally visible cancellation receipts, and process-tree termination confirmation, while retaining single-writer campaign semantics and token-bound release.

Resolving that value beneath a trusted root can therefore select the root's parent even though ordinary slash-prefixed paths appear reduced to a basename. A static property, non-public setter, official `[BindNever]`, local/parameter shadow, property or member reassignment before the sink, local attribute lookalike, or unbound property rejects the path. **Identity and failure boundary.** Unqualified `PageModel` requires the official Razor Pages using and no repository-local `PageModel` declaration; fully qualified and `global::` bases are accepted only when the official namespace is not shadowed. Local inheritance must resolve one simple base type to one `.cs` file at every edge. Duplicate names, qualified unknown intermediates, external bases, cycles, and a ninth edge fail closed. Only public non-static HTTP-verb handlers participate. Official `[NonHandler]` excludes the exact method. `[FromServices]`, `[FromKeyedServices]`, `[BindNever]`, `CancellationToken`, provider/logging interfaces, page/request/response contexts, principals, and other infrastructure-shaped parameters are not remote user values. Comments and ordinary strings are structurally masked before every identity and call decision.

**Flow and compact-call correction.** Synthetic Razor sources only activate a model; they never use the old nearest-source fallback. The host reparses the containing method, calculates which exact parameters or property-derived aliases reach the sink expression or wrapper argument, and clears flow on reassignment. ## 2026-08-05 — Resolve promoted Go methods through embedded concrete structs

**Decision.** Extend the object-authorization receiver graph with exact local concrete method promotion. Parse an embedded field only in one of Go's supported named forms, derive its unqualified field name, and retain whether it embeds `T` or `*T`. Resolve a selector breadth-first from the outer concrete struct. At each depth, count both fields and methods with the requested name: a direct declaration hides deeper names, and a shallow depth is usable only when it contains exactly one method and no competing field. Follow at most eight embedded fields, preserve exact directory, package, import, and exported visibility identity, and record every traversed field as `go-method-receiver-promoted-field` evidence.

**Why.** Go services commonly embed a repository or a repository-bearing layer and call its promoted methods as if they belonged to the service. The previous parser accepted only explicitly named fields, so `service.DeleteInvoice(...)` disappeared even when the complete handler, constructor, local struct graph, method declaration, object flow, and database effect were present. Resolving by outer type and method name would be unsafe because Go selectors choose the unique name at the shallowest depth and because `T`, `*T`, an embedded `T`, and an embedded `*T` expose different method sets. The bounded breadth-first graph reproduces those language rules without inventing dynamic dispatch.

**Selector, method-set, and failure boundary.** Interface satisfaction begins with the actual method set: a value `T` admits value-receiver methods, while `*T` admits value and pointer receivers. Traversing embedded `T` preserves that pointer capability; traversing embedded `*T` makes both receiver forms available to either outer method set. An ordinary concrete variable call is separately allowed to use pointer methods because the modeled binding is addressable. A direct field or method wins before any deeper traversal. Same-depth collisions are ambiguous even when they eventually reach the same receiver type. A cycle, ninth edge, unresolved or external embedded type, embedded interface, generic or unsupported declaration, inaccessible unexported method, duplicate method, missing local struct identity, or pointer/value mismatch rejects resolution. No external package or compiler approximation is inferred.

**Receiver-state correction.** A promoted pointer method exists in the static method set even when the embedded pointer is nil, but such a call cannot reach the recorded database effect. Each embedded pointer edge therefore creates an exact receiver requirement on the constructor/binding graph. The new nil-pointer controls exposed a terminal composition defect: wrapper-edge construction carried call-site requirements, but direct matching of the final callee enforced only requirements already stored inside the callee summary. Direct matching now combines the target call's requirements with every callee requirement prefixed by the promoted receiver path before accepting the binding. This fix applies uniformly to promoted, explicit concrete-field, and narrowed interface-field dispatch.

**Executable and regression evidence.** Expand the strict Go authorization manifest from sixty-eight to seventy cases with paired Go 1.26 modules. `Service` embeds `RepositoryLayer`, which embeds `*store.Store`; an exact constructor initializes the pointer before the handler invokes the promoted deletion. The control retains both embeddings and the constructor but adds the context-derived account predicate; its witness rejects the victim and deletes an owned invoice. Focused positives cover nested cross-package concrete calls, value and pointer interface satisfaction, addressable value calls, and shallow direct-method precedence. Negatives cover uninitialized embedded pointers under both interface and concrete calls, same-depth method ambiguity, a shallower field collision, cyclic pointer embeddings, an unresolved external embedding, a value that lacks the required pointer method set, and exact acceptance at eight promotion edges with rejection at nine.

**Consequence.** Exact object, principal, and protected-effect flow now survives a common Go composition boundary without broad method-name guessing, and nil embedded pointers no longer masquerade as executable sinks at a terminal match. ## 2026-08-05 — Canonicalize Go interface signatures across package boundaries

**Decision.** Compare distinct named basic interfaces with bounded canonical Go type identities instead of whitespace-normalized source text. Parse each complete method signature into canonical parameter and result lists, discard parameter/result names, expand grouped declarations, normalize the predeclared aliases `byte` and `rune`, and structurally identify supported pointers, slices, numeric-length arrays, maps, directional channels, function types, empty interfaces, named types, and bounded named-type arguments. Admit a conversion only when every target method has the same canonical signature in the source; exported method identity may cross packages, while unexported method identity additionally requires the same declaring package.

**Why.** Go interface method identity ignores parameter names, and imported type identity depends on the imported package rather than the spelling of a file-local alias. The previous raw comparison therefore rejected legal same-package cross-file and cross-package conversions such as `DeleteInvoice(requestContext ctx.Context, connection *database.DB, invoiceID string) (failure error)` to `DeleteInvoice(context.Context, *sql.DB, string) error`, even though Go proves them identical. Go's assignability and conversion rules permit an interface source whose method set implements the target, and this conversion changes the static type without changing the carried dynamic value. Canonical identities preserve that exact semantic edge. The approach also follows CodeQL's distinction between value-preserving local flow and configurable taint steps, while retaining the explicit propagator and failure semantics emphasized by Semgrep's data-flow model.

**Identity and failure boundary.** Explicit aliases bind directly to import paths. One precomputed local-module index maps each import path to its unique package clause, avoiding a repository rescan for every import. ## 2026-08-04 — Bind Go receiver fields to constructor-selected instances

**Decision.** Extend Go object-authorization method summaries with receiver-instance requirements. A keyed constructor composite may initialize a named pointer or basic-interface field from one exact constructor parameter or direct concrete expression. The caller resolves the actual argument, carries its exact module/package/type and pointer identity through bounded aliases and assignments, and stores that proof under the returned receiver's field map. A summary through that field is usable only when its instance requirements are satisfied at the final call site.

**Why.** Pointer and interface declarations identify static access paths but do not prove non-nil state or a runtime implementation. Constructors are the common place where Go programs establish that state. Enumerating every visible interface implementation without carrying the selected argument would create false positives; choosing a single visible implementation would create false negatives and unstable results. Parameterized receiver requirements let the graph retain all exact alternatives and defer narrowing until the concrete constructor call provides the missing instance fact.

**Constructor and method-set boundary.** Parse only keyed fields in the constructor's single exact local composite result. A source may be one non-reassigned parameter or a directly resolvable composite, allocation, interface conversion, or nested exact constructor within the existing eight-step constructor bound. Concrete fields require exact static parameter and field identity. Interface parameters must resolve to the same local basic interface when both sides are interfaces. The call must satisfy exact ordinary or minimum variadic arity, and a bare argument may use only a live exact binding. An interface-held value cannot select a pointer-only method; a pointer may select pointer or value methods. Missing fields, nil or unbound values, wrong types, reassigned parameters, ambiguous constructors or structs, and unsatisfied instance requirements fail closed.

**Summary and ambiguity boundary.** A field edge records both the static declaration and a field-path requirement. Interface dispatch may produce several exact receiver-specific summaries; ambiguous paths without instance requirements still fail closed. Candidate grouping retains multiple alternatives only when every alternative is guarded by a concrete receiver requirement. Final matching traverses the constructor-produced field map, compares canonical directory, package, type, and pointer mode, and emits only satisfied summaries. Constructor-field proof is added to the evidence path, and unused implementations never appear in the finding.

## 2026-08-04 — Close Go collection authorization through exact Rows iteration

**Decision.** Extend the typed Go object-authorization model from single-row `QueryRow` disclosure into collection access through exact standard-library `Query`/`QueryContext`, returned `Rows` identity, conditional `Next`, `Scan`, and response use of scanned data. Emit a distinct collection-response sink so list/export impact, single-record impact, and mutations remain independently reviewable. Accept security-named request keys as possible selected objects while continuing to require authenticated-principal provenance for any security predicate claimed as authorization evidence.

**Why.** Go documents that DB, Tx, and Conn `Query` methods return `*Rows`, that the cursor begins before its first record, that `Next` prepares a row for reading, and that every `Rows.Scan` must be preceded by `Next`. Query execution, cursor creation, or a same-named scan therefore does not prove collection disclosure. OWASP API1:2023 explicitly uses a shop revenue listing selected by a request path as a BOLA example, so restricting the model to at-most-one-row APIs left a material false-negative family. Conversely, broadly treating any later `Scan` or writer as closure would discard the exact object-lifecycle discipline that makes the single-record model useful.

**Cursor and disclosure boundary.** Extend fixed-query positions to `Query` at argument zero and `QueryContext` at argument one on proven DB, Tx, or Conn receivers. Store only the exact first returned value as a `Rows` candidate, preserve a simple non-reassigned local cursor alias, and clear identity when an assigned name is replaced. Require `Next` on that cursor in an `if` or `for` condition before accepting receiver `Scan`; a bare ignored `Next`, a different receiver, a later unrelated bare `Scan`, `Close`, `Err`, or query construction alone is inert. Preserve scanned values and bounded aliases only until one reaches an exact writer/encoder shape. Direct chained `QueryRow(...).Scan(...)` remains supported only when parse and scan share the same line; assigned `Row.Scan` requires the exact returned receiver.

**Object and control boundary.** Any exact `id`, `key`, `uuid`, or suffixed key predicate may select the attacker-chosen object, including names such as `account_id`. Naming does not make request input trusted. A security-dimension predicate becomes `principal-bound-object-query` only when its exact placeholder value traces to `Request.Context().Value` through a principal-related server-owned key; a request header, query, form, path value, or similarly named wrapper argument remains attacker controlled. When several request-derived keys reach one wrapper sink, emit one protected-effect hypothesis rather than duplicate reports by parameter. Preserve positional, numbered, and named placeholder-to-argument mapping and require the reviewer to validate the exact collection, action, denial behavior, and returned properties.

**Executable and regression evidence.** Expand the strict authorization manifest from two to four cases with paired Go 1.26 collection modules. The positive sends `victim-project` through a typed path source and one unique wrapper into `SELECT secret FROM invoices WHERE project_id = ?`, then traverses `QueryContext`, `Rows.Next`, `Rows.Scan`, and `io.WriteString`; a deterministic offline driver proves disclosure of both victim secrets. The control preserves the route, project ID, wrapper, cursor loop, scan, and response but adds `account_id = ?` bound from the authenticated request context; its driver proves the attacker sees no victim data and still receives its owned project record. Sixteen focused tests cover the four-case manifest, exact single and collection paths, Query/QueryContext roles, cursor aliases, Next/Scan/disclosure closure, ignored Next, missing or unrelated Scan, generic responses, context-only controls, security-named object keys, DB/Tx/Conn identity, wrappers, deduplication, reassignment, fixed maps, comments/strings, and reviewer guidance. Whole-instance or field reassignment clears the old flow. For direct operations, a recognized custom rewriter may follow only exact leading pgx query options and closes at `Exec`, `Query`, or `QueryRow`. For batches it must be the first queued option, and the rewritten path remains deferred until the exact non-reassigned batch reaches `SendBatch`.
